STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r13.claim: The sūrah celebrates God and the angels blessing the Prophet and commands believers to invoke blessings upon him.
STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r13.anchor: declares that God and His angels invoke blessings upon the Prophet and enjoins the believers to do so as well

STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r15.claim: Love for the Prophet and his family has long been considered foundational to faith, based on these verses and many hadiths.
STUDYQURAN:33:intro/r15.anchor: love for the Prophet and his family has long been regarded as a foundational component of faith

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r11.claim: Most readers put “His angels” in the accusative; Ibn Abbas and a transmission from Abu Amr read it nominative, with competing grammatical explanations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وملائكته نصبا وابن عباس، وعبد الوارث عن أبي عمرو: رفعا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r12.claim: The nominative reading is parsed by Kufans (except al-Farra’) as coordinated with the position of “inna’s” noun, while Basrans supply an omitted predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p501/r12.anchor: فعند الكوفيين غير الفراء هو عطف على موضع اسم إن، والفراء يشترط خفاء إعراب اسم إن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r1.claim: Exegetes differ over whether prayer upon the Prophet is obligatory or recommended; if obligatory, one view requires it once in every gathering when he is mentioned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r1.anchor: والظاهر وجوب الصلاة والسلام عليه، وقيل: سنة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r2.claim: A report says companions knew how to greet the Prophet but asked how to pray for him; he taught a formula invoking blessing on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p502/r2.anchor: وروي أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال قوم من الصحابة

DURR-FULL:v4p615/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p615/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p615/r6.claim: Two angels at the lips record only blessings upon the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v4p615/r6.anchor: وملكان على شفتيك ليس يحفظان عليك إلا الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r3.claim: The command for believers to send prayer on the Prophet means to ask God to send prayer on him, just as the angels do.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r3.anchor: أي ادعوا الله بأن يصلي عليه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.claim: A report says that when the verse about God's and the angels' prayer on the Prophet was revealed, Abū Bakr said that every honor granted the Prophet was shared with them; then 'their greeting' was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p555/r6.anchor: ويروى أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى : { إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبى } ( الأحزاب : 56 ) قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r1.claim: After respect rules for the Prophet's private household, this verse completes the account of his honor in public: he is honored in the highest assembly by God and the angels, and in the lower assembly believers must honor him.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r1.anchor: لما أمر الله المؤمنين بالاستئذان وعدم النظر إلى وجوه نسائه احتراما

RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r2.claim: Ṣalāt means prayer or supplication in Arabic, but that sense cannot apply to God because supplication asks a third party to benefit someone; al-Shāfiʿī says the word is used with distinct meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r2.anchor: وهذا المعنى غير معقول في حق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r3.claim: In 33:43 God is named separately before the angels, while here God and angels share a plural predicate; naming one before a conjunct signals precedence, like saying the king enters and another, and exalts the Prophet as the focal recipient of prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r3.anchor: كما أن الملك إذا قال يدخل فلان وفلان أيضا يفهم منه تقديم

RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r4.claim: For the Prophet, God's prayer is foundational and the angels join it as something incumbent or recommended whether or not God has prayed; for believers, the angels' prayer does not have that same status.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r4.anchor: فقال في حق النبي عليه السلام إنهم يصلون إشارة إلى أنه في الصلاة على النبي عليه السلام كالأصل

RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r5.claim: Because the command entails obligation, al-Shāfiʿī takes this verse to require prayer upon the Prophet in the tashahhud; Razi says it is not obligatory outside it.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196/r5.anchor: هذا دليل على مذهب الشافعي لأن الأمر للوجوب فتجب الصلاة على النبي عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r1.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r1.claim: When asked how to pray upon him, the Prophet taught the formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family, and to grant them blessing as He did them; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r1.anchor: النبي عليه السلام كيف نصلي عليك يا رسول الله ؟ فقال : ( قولوا اللهم صل على محمد

RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r2.claim: Believers' prayers do not meet a need of the Prophet, just as he needs no angelic prayer; they express reverence and, out of mercy for believers, earn them reward.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r2.anchor: كما أن الله تعالى أوجب علينا ذكر نفسه ولا حاجة له إليه

RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r3.claim: The Prophet said that whoever prays upon him once receives ten prayers from God; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r3.anchor: من صلى علي مرة صلى الله عليه عشرا

RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is not left under the community's favor for praying for him, since God directs him to pray for the community, whose comfort is in his prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r4.anchor: لم يترك الله النبي عليه السلام تحت منة أمته بالصلاة حتى عوضهم منه بأمره بالصلاة على الأمة

RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r5.claim: The command to salute is obligatory, and because it is not required outside prayer, the salutation Peace be upon you, O Prophet is required in tashahhud; this opposes those who deny its obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r5.anchor: أمر فيجب ولم يجب في غير الصلاة فيجب فيها وهو قولنا السلام عليك أيها النبي في التشهد

RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r6.claim: The verbal noun emphasizes completing the salutation; the prayer is not reinforced with the same emphasis because the preceding clause already confirms it.
RAZI-FULL:v25p196#2/r6.anchor: ولم يؤكد الصلاة بهذا التأكيد لأنها كانت مؤكدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r1.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying Satan moves through a human like blood, and people should narrow those paths through hunger; no chain or grading is supplied here.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r1.anchor: إن الشيطان ليجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم ألا فضيقوا مجاريه بالجوع

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r2.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that if satans did not hover over Adam's children's hearts, they would see the kingdom of the heavens; no chain or grading is supplied.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r2.anchor: وقال عليه السلام لولا أن الشياطين يحومون على قلوب بني آدم لنظروا إلى ملكوت السموات

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r3.speaker: ومن الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r3.claim: Some interpreters say these reports cannot be literal: devils entering people's insides would require bodily passages to expand or bodies to interpenetrate.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r3.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : هذه الأخبار لا بد من تأويلها لأنه يمتنع حملها على ظواهرها

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r4.speaker: ومن الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r4.claim: A second objection says devils intensely hate religious people; if they could enter humans, they would inflict especially great harm on them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r4.anchor: أن العداوة الشديدة حاصلة بينه وبين أهل الدين فلو قدر على هذا النفوذ فلم لا يخصهم بمزيد الضرر

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r5.speaker: ومن الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r5.claim: A third objection argues that because Satan is created from fire, his entry into a body should feel like fire inside it, yet it is not felt.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r5.anchor: أن الشيطان مخلوق من النار فلو دخل في داخل البدن لصار كأنه نفذ النار في داخل البدن

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r6.speaker: ومن الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r6.claim: A fourth objection says devils love sin and disbelief, yet people implore them to produce vice without seeing an effect, so neither their hostility nor friendship appears to harm or help.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r6.anchor: أن الشياطين يحبون المعاصي وأنواع الكفر والفسق ثم إنا نتضرع بأعظم الوجوه إليهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r7.speaker: مثبتو الشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r7.claim: The affirmers answer that if devils are immaterial souls, the objection about bodily passages disappears; if they are subtle bodies like light or air, it also disappears.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r7.anchor: وأجاب مثبتو الشياطين عن السؤال الأول بان على القول بأنها نفوس مجردة فالسؤال زائل

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r8.speaker: مثبتو الشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r8.claim: They answer the second objection by saying God and His angels may prevent devils from harming learned human beings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r8.anchor: وعن الثاني لا يبعد أن يقال : إن الله وملائكته يمنعونهم عن إيذاء علماء البشر

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r9.speaker: مثبتو الشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r9.claim: They answer that God could make a fire harmless, as He commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Abraham, so the same is possible here.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r9.anchor: وعن الثالث أنه لما جاز أن يقول الله تعالى لنار إبراهيم : ﴿ يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r10.speaker: مثبتو الشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r10.claim: They answer the final objection by saying devils choose freely and may commit some vices but not others.
RAZI-FULL:v1p76/r10.anchor: وعن الرابع أن الشياطين مختارون ولعلهم يفعلون بعض القبائح دون بعض

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r1.claim: This often cited verse is central to understanding the Prophet's place in Islam.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r1.anchor: This frequently cited verse is among the most important in the Quran for understanding the place of the Prophet in Islam

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r2.claim: In its immediate context, the verse explains why the Prophet should be obeyed, is a beautiful example and a luminous lamp, and has distinctive marital and family rulings.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r2.anchor: it answers questions one might ask of the previous verses: why the Prophet should be obeyed

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r3.claim: Invoke blessings translates ṣallā/yuṣallī, from the same root as ṣalāh, prayer.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r3.anchor: Invoke blessings translates the verb ṣallā/yuṣallī, which is from the same rootas ṣalāh

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r4.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r4.claim: Commentators distinguish the senses: God's ṣalāh is loving Mercy, while the angels' ṣalāh is seeking forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r4.anchor: God’s ṣalāh is loving Mercy and that of the angels is seeking forgiveness (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r5.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r5.claim: Human beings invoke blessings by supplicating for the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r5.anchor: Human beings then invoke blessings by supplicating for the Prophet (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r6.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r6.claim: Human beings also invoke blessings by following and loving the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r6.anchor: by following him and loving him (Su)

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r7.claim: When Companions asked how to bless him after learning the greeting of peace, the Prophet taught a supplication asking God to bless and shower grace on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r7.anchor: To which he answered,“O God! Bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as Thou hast blessed Abraham

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r8.speaker: al-Ālūsī
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī says asking God to bless the Prophet acknowledges that people can do no more than request God's blessings.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r8.anchor: the manner in which human beings invoke blessings upon the Prophet, by calling for God’s Blessings upon him, means that they are in fact realizing their inability

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r9.speaker: K
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r9.claim: Metaphysically, only God invokes blessings upon the Prophet; human prayer participates in and affirms the Divine Act.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r9.anchor: in all modes of asking blessing upon the Prophet, it is only God Who invokes blessings upon him (K)

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r10.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r10.claim: The Prophet reports Gabriel's message that God blesses tenfold anyone in the community who blesses the Prophet and returns peace tenfold to anyone who greets him.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r10.anchor: No member of thy community invokes blessings upon thee but that I bless him tenfold

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r11.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r11.claim: The Prophet calls a person miserly if his name is mentioned in that person's presence and the person does not bless him.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r11.anchor: The miser is one who when I am mentioned in his presence does not invoke blessings upon me

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r12.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r12.claim: When a man supplicated hastily, the Prophet instructed him to praise God first, bless the Prophet next, and then supplicate as he wished.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r12.anchor: When one makes supplication, let him begin by praising God. Then let him invoke blessings upon the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r13.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r13.claim: ʿUmar says a supplication remains suspended between Heaven and earth until blessings are invoked upon the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r13.anchor: A supplication is suspended between Heaven and earth and does not ascend any further until you invoke blessings upon your Prophet

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r14.claim: Blessing the Prophet benefits believers rather than the Prophet, so the verse is understood as a command to all believers.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r14.anchor: invoking blessings upon the Prophet is not a benefit for the Prophet, but for the believers themselves

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r15.speaker: IK, Q, R
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r15.claim: Some consider blessing the Prophet commendable, while others consider it obligatory.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r15.anchor: Some say that invoking blessings upon the Prophet is a commendable deed

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r16.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r16.claim: Among those who regard it as obligatory, some require blessings once in a lifetime, while others require them in every prayer.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r16.anchor: Some maintain that its being obligatory may simply mean that such blessings must be invoked at some point during the course of one’s life

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r17.speaker: Imam al-Shāfiʿī and many followers of his legal tradition
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r17.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and many followers hold that a prayer is valid only if blessings are invoked upon the Prophet in every prayer.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r17.anchor: According to Imam al-Shāfiʿī and many followers of his legal tradition, one must invoke blessings upon the Prophet in every prayer

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r18.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r18.claim: Blessing the Prophet draws one nearer to God: increased invocation engenders love for the Prophet, then love for God, whose love draws the person to His Presence.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r18.anchor: invoking blessings upon the Prophet is essential for drawing closer to God

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r19.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r19.claim: Greetings of peace mean the standard Muslim greeting and also being at peace with the Prophet, accepting his message, yielding to him, and submitting to the Divine Law.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r19.anchor: refers to the standard Muslim greeting, “Peace be upon you,” but it also indicates being at peace with the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r20.claim: Islamic tradition says all creation prostrates to God and also extends greetings of peace to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r20.anchor: trees, stones, and all creation prostrate to God (see 16:40; 22:18; 55:6), so too do they extend greetings of peace

STUDYQURAN:33:56/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r21.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r21.claim: ʿAlī reports that on a walk around Makkah, every rock and tree greeted the Prophet with peace.
STUDYQURAN:33:56/r21.anchor: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib is reported to have said, “I went out with the Prophet through the environs of Makkah. Every rock and tree welcomed him

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r1.claim: People of unveiling divide angels into those who descended from the spirit world into subtle bodies and those who remained disembodied in the spirit world.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الملائكة عند أهل الكشف من أكابر أهل الله على قسمين

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r2.claim: The first angelic class has subtle bodies, includes the earthly and heavenly angels, and was commanded to prostrate to Adam.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r2.anchor: قسم تنزلوا من مرتبة الأرواح إلى مرتبة الأجسام فلهم أجسام لطيفة

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r3.claim: The second class, the absorbed angels, has no bodily covering or awareness of self or other beings because it is wholly immersed in witnessing God; it was not commanded to prostrate.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r3.anchor: وهم المهيمون الذين أشير إليهم بقوله تعالى : {أم كنت من العالين} وهم غير مأمورين بالسجود

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r4.claim: Humans surpass both angelic classes in state and perfection because they were created by the hands of Beauty and Majesty, while angels were created by Beauty alone.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r4.anchor: والإنسان أفضل من هذين القسمين في شرف الحال ورتبة الكمال لأنه مخلوق بقبضتي الجمال والجلال

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r5.claim: Love entails trial in the world: Adam's descent and worldly hardship are forms of divine education and effects of Majesty.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r5.anchor: العشق يقتضي المحنة وموطنها الدنيا ولذا أهبط آدم من الجنة والمحنة من باب التربية

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r6.claim: The angels meant here are initially the embodied first class, who share bodily existence with believers; the honor of the verse also calls for taking the reference generally.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بالملائكة ههنا هو القسم الأول لأنهم يشاركون مؤمني البشر في الجمال والوجود الجسماني

BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r7.claim: God and the angels attend to the Prophet's good, display his honor, and magnify his status; God's salat is mercy and the angels' is supplication and seeking forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v7p169#2/r7.anchor: يعتنون بما فيه خيره وصلاح أمره ويهتمون بإظهار شرفه وتعظيم شأنه

BURSEVI:v7p170/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p170/r1.claim: Yusalluna is used by general metaphor, since a homonym cannot simultaneously carry both senses, whether or not those senses conflict.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r1.anchor: فقوله يصلون محمول على عموم المجاز إذ لا يجوز إرادة معنيي المشترك معا

BURSEVI:v7p170/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r2.speaker: القهستاني
BURSEVI:v7p170/r2.claim: Al-Qahistani assigns mercy to God's salat, forgiveness to angels, worship and supplication to humans and jinn, and glorification to birds and vermin.

BURSEVI:v7p170/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p170/r3.claim: Salat is a verbal noun from tasliya, while the ordinary ritual prayer has only the form salat, not a verbal noun tasliya.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r3.anchor: اسم من التصلية وكلاهما مستعمل بخلاف الصلاة بمعنى أداء الأركان

BURSEVI:v7p170/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p170/r4.claim: Some say God's salat is mercy for others but added honor for the Prophet; salat is special while mercy is general, as the verse pairing them shows.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الصلاة من الله تعالى بمعنى الرحمة لغير النبي عليه السلام وبمعنى التشريف

BURSEVI:v7p170/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p170/r5.claim: Some distinguish the effects: God grants the Prophet praise and support, angels praise and assist him, and believers seek his intercession and follow his Sunnah; for others these are mercy, forgiveness, and supplication.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : صلوات الله على غير النبي رحمة وعلى النبي ثناء ومدحة قولا وتوفيق وتأييد فعلا

BURSEVI:v7p170/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p170/r6.claim: Believers too should attend to the Prophet with blessings, since they are more deserving of this.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r6.anchor: اعتنوا أنتم أيضا بذلك فإنكم أولى به

BURSEVI:v7p170/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r7.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p170/r7.claim: A hadith is cited directing people who bless the Prophet to include others; Bursevi says omitting this leaves the blessing incomplete.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r7.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام : "إذا صليتم علي فعمموا" وإلا فقد نقصت الصلاة عليه

BURSEVI:v7p170/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r8.speaker: السخاوي
BURSEVI:v7p170/r8.claim: Al-Sakhawi says he did not find the cited hadith with that wording; it might mean praying for the Prophet and God's other prophets, whom God sent as He sent him.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r8.anchor: وقال الإمام السخاوي في المقاصد الحسنة لم أقف عليه أي : على هذا الحديث بهذا اللفظ

BURSEVI:v7p170/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p170/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p170/r9.claim: The formula chooses Allahumma because it is a comprehensive name denoting divinity and suits the Prophet, who gathers the qualities of perfection and mysteries of Beauty and Majesty.
BURSEVI:v7p170/r9.anchor: وخص اللهم ولم يقل يا رب ويا رحمن صل لأنه اسم جامع دال على الألوهية

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r1.claim: Blessings raise the Prophet's rank and thereby the community's rank, because a follower's rank depends on the one followed; Rumi expresses this in a cited poem.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r1.anchor: بالصلوات تزيد مرتبة النبي فتزيد مرتبة الأمة لأن مرتبة التابع تابعة لمرتبة المتبوع

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r2.claim: Sending blessings also manifests love, since a person mentions what he loves often.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r2.anchor: وأيضا فيها إثبات المحبة ومن أحب شيئا أكثر ذكره

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r3.claim: Some take the present tense to show angels bless continually; imitating them brings a share of their purity and familiarity with the spiritual world.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : صيغة المضارع يعني : {يصلون} (دلالت بر آن ميكندكه ملائكه يوسته دركفتن صلواتند

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r4.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r4.claim: Sahl al-Tustari calls blessings upon Muhammad the best worship because God and the angels perform it before commanding believers to do so.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r4.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله التستري قدس سره : الصلاة على محمد أفضل العبادات لأن الله تولاها هو وملائكته

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r5.speaker: الصديق الأكبر
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr says blessings erase sins more than cold water extinguishes fire and surpass freeing slaves; greeting the Prophet corresponds to God's greeting, better than a thousand good deeds.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r5.anchor: قال الصديق الأكبر رضي الله عنه : الصلاة عليه أمحق للذنوب من الماء البارد للنار وهي أفضل من عتق الرقاب

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r6.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti urges reverent blessings without imagining they can discharge any measure of the Prophet's due; they instead seek God's mercy through him.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي صل عليه بالأوقار ولا تجعل له في قلبك مقدار

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r7.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r7.claim: A hadith says an angel at the Prophet's grave relays each believer's blessing to him by name and father's name, and God blesses that believer tenfold.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إنملكا أعطاه سمع الخلائق وهو قائم على قبري إذا مت إلى يوم القيامة فليس أحد من أمتي

BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r8.speaker: حديث
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r8.claim: Another hadith says blessings are presented to the Prophet with the sender's name, father's name, tribe, and uncles; proper blessing requires presence of heart and collected attention.
BURSEVI:v7p173#2/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إذا صليتم علي فأحسنوا علي الصلاة فإنكم تعرضون علي بأسمائكم وأسماء آبائكم وعشائركم وأعمامكم"

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r1.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r1.claim: Some spiritual elders say that sending three thousand blessings on Friday night brings a vision of the Prophet in a dream; al-Safi cites this in al-Rashahat.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r1.anchor: وعن بعض الكبار أن من صلى على النبي عليه السلام ليلة الجمعة ثلاثة آلاف رأى في منامه

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r2.claim: When mounting for a journey, say the basmala and takbir, bless the best of humanity, and recite the travel verses.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r2.anchor: بسم الله والله أكبر وصل على محمد خير البشر

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r3.claim: On the Mecca road, say takbir while ascending high ground and send blessings when descending.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r3.anchor: بر بلندى رود تكبير بايد كفت وون روى بنشيب آرد صلوات بايد فرستاد

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r4.claim: Send blessings when touching the Black Stone, at Safa and Marwa, after the talbiya, and while standing at the Sacred Monument.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r4.anchor: وعند استلام الحجر يقول : "اللهم إيمانا بك وتصديقا بكتابك وسنة نبيك" ثم يصلي

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r5.claim: On approaching the Prophet's grave, recite this verse through its end and say صلى الله عليك يا محمد seventy times; an angel replies with the visitor's name and promises the request will not be refused.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r5.anchor: وهفتاد باربكويد صلى الله عليك يا محمد (فرشته ندا كندكه) صلى الله عليك يا فلان

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r6.claim: Blessings are also prescribed between the grave and pulpit, when the Prophet is mentioned or his name is spoken or written, and by a writer both aloud and in writing.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r6.anchor: ويصلي بين القبر والمنبر ويكبر ويدعو

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r7.claim: Begin hadith study and transmission of the Sunnah with a formula of praise, blessing, and peace upon the Prophet, his family, other prophets, and the righteous.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r7.anchor: ويصلي عند ابتداء درس الحديث وتبليغ السنن فيقول

BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r8.claim: Begin admonition and preaching with blessings after praise, since it is a setting for conveying knowledge transmitted from the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v7p179#2/r8.anchor: ويصلي عند ابتداء التذكير والعظة أي : بعد الحمد والثناء لأنه موطن تبليغ العلم

BURSEVI:v7p183#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p183#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p183#2/r1.claim: The source gives a comprehensive blessing formula for Muhammad, his family, wives, and descendants, modeled on God's blessing of Abraham and his family.
BURSEVI:v7p183#2/r1.anchor: اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك النبي الأمي وعلى آل محمد وأزواجه وذريته

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r1.claim: God and His angels bless the Prophet Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه} [الأحزاب: 56] يقول: «يباركون على النبي»

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the prayer of God and the angels as blessing the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه} [الأحزاب: 56] يقول: «يباركون على النبي»

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r3.claim: Alternatively, God’s prayer means mercy, while the angels pray for the Prophet and seek forgiveness; prayer by creatures means supplication in Arabic.
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r3.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يقال: إن معنى ذلك: أن الله يرحم النبي، وتدعو له ملائكته ويستغفرون، وذلك أن الصلاة في كلام العرب من غير الله إنما

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r4.claim: The believers are commanded to supplicate for the Prophet Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r4.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ادعوا لنبي الله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r5.claim: The believers are commanded to greet the Prophet with the Islamic greeting.

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r6.speaker: طلحة
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r6.claim: Talha reports that the Prophet taught a formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family.
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r6.anchor: عن موسى بن طلحة، عن أبيه، قال: أتى رجل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: سمعت الله يقول: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي}

TAB-FULL:v19p175/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r7.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r7.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports asking the Prophet how to pray for him; he taught a formula blessing Muhammad and his family as Abraham and his family were blessed.
TAB-FULL:v19p175/r7.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة، قال: لما نزلت: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما} [الأحزاب: 56]

TAB-FULL:v19p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the people asked how to pray for the Prophet after learning the greeting; the response includes blessing Muhammad and his family as Abraham’s family.
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r1.anchor: فقال: أنبأني من سمع ابن عباس يقول: هكذا أنزل، فقلنا: أو قالوا: يا رسول الله قد علمنا السلام عليك

TAB-FULL:v19p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r2.claim: Ibrahim reports that the response to the people’s question was to ask blessing for Muhammad, God’s servant and messenger, and his household as for Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r2.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن زياد، عن إبراهيم، في قوله {إن الله وملائكته} [الأحزاب: 56] . . الآية، قالوا: يا رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v19p177/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن بشر بن مسعود الأنصاري
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr reports that the Prophet taught asking God to bless and favor Muhammad as He did the family of Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين، عن عبد الرحمن بن بشر بن مسعود الأنصاري، قال: لما نزلت: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه

TAB-FULL:v19p177/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r4.claim: Qatada reports that, when the verse was revealed, the Prophet told them to ask God to bless Muhammad as Abraham and to bless Muhammad as Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما} [الأحزاب: 56] قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v19p177/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r5.claim: Al-Hasan’s formula asks God to place His blessings and favor on Muhammad’s family as He placed them on Abraham’s family.
TAB-FULL:v19p177/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: واللهم اجعل صلواتك وبركاتك على آل محمد، كما جعلتها على إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد

TABATABAI:33:53-56/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r8.claim: The root sense of prayer is inclination or turning toward someone; God’s prayer for the Prophet is an unrestricted bestowal of mercy.
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r8.anchor: أصل الصلاة الانعطاف فصلاته تعالى انعطافه عليه بالرحمة انعطافا مطلقا

TABATABAI:33:53-56/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r9.claim: The angels’ prayer for the Prophet is their turning toward him through praise and seeking forgiveness.
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r9.anchor: وكذلك صلاة الملائكة عليه انعطاف عليه بالتزكية والاستغفار

TABATABAI:33:53-56/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:53-56/r10.claim: Believers’ prayer for the Prophet means supplication for mercy.

TABRISI:33:56-62/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:56-62/r1.claim: The passage supplies a formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family, and to bless them likewise.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r1.anchor: قولوا اللهم صل على محمد وآل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم

TABRISI:33:56-62/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:33:56-62/r2.claim: Ibn Masud urged people to offer a beautiful prayer for the Prophet, since they did not know whether it would be presented to him, and taught a prayer invoking blessings and his praiseworthy station.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: إذا صليتم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:33:56-62/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r3.speaker: أبو بصير
TABRISI:33:56-62/r3.claim: Abu Basir reports Abu Abdillah explaining God's prayer for the Messenger as God's purification of him in the highest heavens.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r3.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال: سألت أبا عبد الله ع عن هذه الآية

TABRISI:33:56-62/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r4.speaker: أبو بصير
TABRISI:33:56-62/r4.claim: Abu Abdillah explained taslim as submitting to the Prophet in matters.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r4.anchor: فقلت قد عرفت صلواتنا عليه فكيف التسليم فقال: هو التسليم له في الأمور

TABRISI:33:56-62/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:56-62/r5.claim: On this explanation, believers submit to the Prophet's commands and exert themselves in obeying everything he orders.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r5.anchor: انقادوا لأوامره وابذلوا الجهد في طاعته وفي جميع ما يأمركم به

TABRISI:33:56-62/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:56-62/r6.claim: An alternative is to greet the Prophet with a supplication, saying, Peace be upon you, Messenger of God.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه سلموا عليه بالدعاء أي قولوا: السلام عليك يا رسول الله

TABRISI:33:56-62/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:56-62/r7.speaker: أبو طلحة
TABRISI:33:56-62/r7.claim: Abu Talha, related by Anas ibn Malik, says the Prophet told him that one prayer upon him earns ten divine blessings, erases ten sins, and adds ten good deeds.
TABRISI:33:56-62/r7.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن أبي طلحة قال: دخلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v8p61/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p61/r1.claim: Most readers put “angels” in the accusative; Ibn Abbas reads it in the nominative, coordinating it with the syntactic position of “Allah” before إن, as in 5:69.
THALABI:v8p61/r1.anchor: إن الله وملائكته قراءة العامة بنصب التاء وقرأ ابن عباس: وملائكته بالرفع عطفا على محل قوله: الله قبل دخول إن، نظيره قوله: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى

THALABI:v8p61/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p61/r2.claim: God and the angels’ prayer for the Prophet means praising him, showing mercy, and praying for him.
THALABI:v8p61/r2.anchor: يصلون على النبي أي يثنون ويترحمون عليه ويدعون له

THALABI:v8p61/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p61/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the angels’ prayer as blessing the Prophet.

THALABI:v8p61/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p61/r4.claim: Believers are to ask mercy and pray for the Prophet, and to greet him with the greeting of Islam.
THALABI:v8p61/r4.anchor: صلوا عليه ترحموا عليه وادعو له وسلموا تسليما وحيوه بتحية الإسلام

THALABI:v8p61/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61/r5.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
THALABI:v8p61/r5.claim: After the verse was revealed, Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra and others asked how to pray for the Prophet; he taught the formula asking blessings on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
THALABI:v8p61/r5.anchor: حدثني كعب بن عجرة قال: لما نزلت إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي ... قلنا: يا رسول الله قد علمنا السلام عليك، فكيف الصلاة عليك؟ قال: «قل: اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم

THALABI:v8p61#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v8p61#2/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports that, when asked how to pray for him, the Prophet taught asking for blessing on Muhammad, his family, and his servant and messenger status, as on Abraham.
THALABI:v8p61#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله هذا السلام قد علمنا، فكيف الصلاة عليك؟ قال: «قولوا اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك كما صليت على إبراهيم

THALABI:v8p61#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61#2/r2.speaker: أبو حميد الساعدي
THALABI:v8p61#2/r2.claim: Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi reports that the Prophet taught a formula including Muhammad’s wives and descendants, asking that they be blessed as Abraham’s family was.
THALABI:v8p61#2/r2.anchor: أخبرني أبو حميد الساعدي أنهم قالوا:

THALABI:v8p61#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61#2/r3.speaker: أبو مسعود الأنصاري
THALABI:v8p61#2/r3.claim: Abu Masʿud al-Ansari reports that the Prophet taught blessing Muhammad and his family as Abraham’s family was blessed throughout the worlds, ending with the greeting already taught.
THALABI:v8p61#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري أنه قال: أتانا رسول الله صلى الله عليه ونحن جلوس في مجلس سعد بن عبادة، فقال له بشير بن [سعد] : أمرنا الله أن نصلي عليك يا رسول الله، فكيف نصلي عليك؟

THALABI:v8p61#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p61#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v8p61#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud urges believers to perfect their prayer for the Prophet because they do not know whether it is presented to him, then gives an extended prayer asking for mercy, blessing, and the Praised Station.
THALABI:v8p61#2/r4.anchor: عن الأسود قال: قال عبد الله: إذا صليتم على النبي صلى الله عليه فأحسنوا الصلاة عليه، فإنكم لا تدرون لعل ذلك يعرض عليه

THALABI:v8p62/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p62/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v8p62/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet calls the meaning hidden knowledge: two appointed angels ask God’s forgiveness for anyone who prays for him, and ask that forgiveness be withheld from one who does not; God and the angels say “Amen.”
THALABI:v8p62/r1.anchor: عن أم الحسن، عن أبيها قالوا: يا رسول الله أرأيت قول الله تعالى: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي فقال النبي (عليه السلام) : هذا من العلم المكنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's ṣalāt is mercy for the Prophet and the angels' ṣalāt is praying for mercy for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد إن الله يرحم النبي والملائكة يدعون له بالرحمة (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says God's ṣalāt means forgiveness for the Prophet, while the angels' ṣalāt means seeking forgiveness for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: أما صلاة الرب فالمغفرة (¬8) للنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- وأما صلاة الملائكة (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the believers' prayer for the Prophet as supplication that God show him mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ادعوا له بالرحمة (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r4.claim: Muqatil explains the command as greeting the Prophet; saying peace be upon him or asking God to keep him safe fulfills it, and combining prayer and greeting fulfills both commands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: استغفروا {وسلموا تسليما} يعني: التسليم (¬2) فيجوز أن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r5.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r5.claim: Ka'b ibn Ujra reports that after this verse the Companions asked how to pray for the Prophet, since they already knew the greeting in tashahhud; he taught them the formula asking blessing for Muhammad and his family as for Abraham and his family.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r5.anchor: وروي عن كعب بن عجرة أنه قال لما نزلت هذه الآية: قلنا يا رسول الله، قد علمنا السلام عليك، فكيف الصلاة عليك؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r6.speaker: الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r6.claim: Al-Shafi'i says a ritual prayer is not valid in the law without invoking blessing and greeting upon the Messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p288#2/r6.anchor: ولهذا قال الشافعي -رضي الله عنه-: لا تصح صلاة في الشريعة إلا بالصلاة على رسول الله والسلام عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r1.claim: God’s ṣalāt is His praise and mercy for the Prophet, while the angels’ ṣalāt is their supplication for him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r1.anchor: الله تعالى يثني على النبي ويرحمه، والملائكة يدعون له

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r2.claim: Believers are to say, “O God, bless Muhammad and grant him peace.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:56-59/r2.anchor: قولوا: اللهم صل على محمد وسلم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains God's ṣalāt as forgiving the Prophet and the angels' ṣalāt as their seeking forgiveness for him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r1.anchor: يعني: أن الله يغفر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتستغفر له الملائكة، هذا تفسير السدي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r2.claim: The believers are commanded to seek forgiveness for the Prophet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r2.anchor: {يأيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه} [الأحزاب: 56] ، يعني: استغفروا له

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r3.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r3.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports that, when asked how to pray for him after learning the greeting, the Prophet taught the formula invoking blessings and favor on Muḥammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، قال: جاءني كعب بن عجرة، فقال لي: ألا أهدي لك هدية؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r4.speaker: أبو طلحة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r4.claim: Abū Ṭalḥa reports that Gabriel brought the Prophet glad tidings: one blessing on him earns ten blessings from God, or a like response.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، عن أبي طلحة قال: دفعت ذات يوم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقلت: يا رسول الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that an angel assigned to the Prophet asks God to bless the servant who invokes blessings on Muḥammad.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r5.anchor: وحدثني حماد الكلبي، عن حماد، عن إبراهيم، عن عبد الله بن مسعود أن ملكا موكلا بالنبي عليه السلام

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the Messenger urged people to invoke blessings on him frequently on Friday.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r6.anchor: وحدثني المبارك بن فضالة، عن الحسن، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أكثروا الصلاة علي يوم الجمعة»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r7.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports the Prophet urging Friday blessings because angels witness that day and every blessing reaches him wherever its sender is; the report then asks how it reaches him after burial.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p735/r7.anchor: عن عبادة بن نسي، عن أبي الدرداء، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أكثروا الصلاة علي يوم الجمعة

QASHANI:33:56-57/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:56-57/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:56-57/r1.claim: God and the angels' blessing of the Prophet is support, confirmations, and the outpouring of perfections; in every respect, with or without intermediaries, God is the true source of blessing.
QASHANI:33:56-57/r1.anchor: بالإمداد والتأييدات والإفاضة للكمالات فالمصلي في الحقيقة هو الله تعالى جميعا وتفصيلا بواسطة وغير واسطة

QASHANI:33:56-57/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:56-57/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:56-57/r2.claim: Believers bless him in a particular, detailed way by accepting his guidance and perfection and loving his essence and attributes, thereby supporting and completing the flow of grace.
QASHANI:33:56-57/r2.anchor: وحقيقة صلاتهم عليه قبولهم لهدايته وكماله ومحبتهم لذاته وصفاته فإنها إمداد له منهم وتكميل وتعميم للفيض

QASHANI:33:56-57/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:56-57/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:56-57/r3.claim: The prayer God bless Muhammad expresses love and purity; salutation means treating him as free of defect while completing and affecting the believers' own selves, which is their prayer for peace upon him.
QASHANI:33:56-57/r3.anchor: وتسليمهم جعلهم إياه بريئا من النقص والآفة في تكميل نفوسهم

ELMALILI:33:56/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r1.claim: God honors the Prophet through mercy and bounty; the angels honor him through prayers for forgiveness and service, continually.

ELMALILI:33:56/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r2.claim: The divine and angelic prayers for the Prophet bring divine grace to believers, as stated in 33:43.
ELMALILI:33:56/r2.anchor: Bu sayede yukarıda هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَلِّى عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتُهُۥ لِيُخْرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ buyurulduğu üzere mü’minlere feyz-i ilâhî inmektedir.

ELMALILI:33:56/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r3.claim: Believers should invoke God's blessings, mercy, and bounty for the Prophet and honor him with salutations, using familiar prayer formulas.
ELMALILI:33:56/r3.anchor: Sizler ona salât ü selâm getirin, selâmlayarak teslim olun ،اَللّهُ َّم صَ ِّل عَلَى مُحَ َّمد

ELMALILI:33:56/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r4.claim: Salām may also mean not hurting the Prophet, submitting to him, and obeying him.
ELMALILI:33:56/r4.anchor: Ve bir mânaya göre hiç incitmeyerek teslim olun, inkıyad edin.

ELMALILI:33:56/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r5.claim: The verse makes prayers for the Prophet obligatory; the author prefers the sound view that this duty recurs whenever his name is mentioned.
ELMALILI:33:56/r5.anchor: Bu âyet gösterir ki Peygamber’e salavat getirmek farzdır. Ancak tekrarına taarruz yoktur. Sahih olan budur ki ismi zikrolundukça vâcib olur.

ELMALILI:33:56/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r6.speaker: Prophet
ELMALILI:33:56/r6.claim: The Prophet warns that the man who hears his name mentioned but does not pray for him is disgraced.
ELMALILI:33:56/r6.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm buyurmuştur ki: “رَغِمَ أَنْفُ رَجُلٍ ذُكِرْتُ عِنْدَهُ

ELMALILI:33:56/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r7.speaker: Prophet
ELMALILI:33:56/r7.claim: A report says two angels ask God to forgive anyone who prays for the Prophet when he is mentioned, and ask that God not forgive anyone who omits it; God and the angels say amen.
ELMALILI:33:56/r7.anchor: Yine buyurmuştur ki: “Allah teâlâ bana iki melek müvekkel kıldı, ben bir müslimin yanında anıldım da bana salavat getirdi mi

ELMALILI:33:56/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r8.claim: Some hold that repeated mention in one sitting requires only one prayer for the Prophet, by analogy with a prostration verse.
ELMALILI:33:56/r8.anchor: Bazıları da zikri tekerrür etse bile bir mecliste bir kere vâcib olur demiştir. Nitekim secde âyetinde böyledir.

ELMALILI:33:56/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r9.claim: He also says prayers for the Prophet are obligatory at both the beginning and end of every supplication.
ELMALILI:33:56/r9.anchor: Kezâlik her duanın evvelinde ve âhirinde de vâcibdir.

ELMALILI:33:56/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r10.claim: For Hanafis, the prayer formula on Muḥammad and his family in ritual prayer is sunnah, not one of the obligatory elements.
ELMALILI:33:56/r10.anchor: diye salavat okumak biz Hanefiyyece namazın vâcibâtından değildir, sünnettir.

ELMALILI:33:56/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r11.speaker: İbrâhim Neha‘î
ELMALILI:33:56/r11.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī reports that the Companions could suffice with the tashahhud's greeting to the Prophet.
ELMALILI:33:56/r11.anchor: İbrâhim Neha‘î’den mervîdir: “Ashâb-ı kirâm teşehhüddeki اَل َّسلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيـ ُّهَا الن َّبِ ُّي وَرَحْمَةُ االلهِ وَبـَرَكَاتُهُ ile iktifâ edebilirlerdi” demiştir.

ELMALILI:33:56/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r12.speaker: İmâm Şâfi‘î
ELMALILI:33:56/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that prayers for the Prophet are a necessary condition for the validity of ritual prayer.
ELMALILI:33:56/r12.anchor: İmâm Şâfi‘î hazretleri “namazın cevâzı için salavat şarttır, vâcibdir” demiştir.

ELMALILI:33:56/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r13.claim: When the Companions asked how to offer prayers for him, the Prophet taught the formula recited in ritual prayer.
ELMALILI:33:56/r13.anchor: Ashâb sormuşlar: “yâ Resûlallah, selâm vermeyi biliyoruz, fakat salâtı nasıl getireceğiz?” demişler, o vakit namazda okunan salavat duası tâlim buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:33:56/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:56/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:56/r14.claim: Praying for non-prophets alongside the Prophet is permitted, but doing so independently is disliked because it is conventionally a prophetic distinction; the honorific ʿazza wa-jalla is not used for him.
ELMALILI:33:56/r14.anchor: Peygamberlerden mâ‘adâsına salavat tebe‘an câiz olursa da istiklâlen mekruhtur. Çünkü örfte peygamberlerin şi‘ârıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r1.claim: The root sense of salāt is putting something to fire or roasting; the author connects turning toward God with presenting oneself to Him, and turning away with putting oneself over fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r1.anchor: salât kelimesinin kök mânası “ateşe tutmak, kızartmak”tır. İnsan kendini ya Allah’a yöneltir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r2.claim: As a religious term, human salāt means either supplication generally or the formal prayer, the latter being the best way to give oneself to God and present oneself before Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r2.anchor: kulların “salât”ı iki mâna ifade etmektedir: 1. Genel olarak dua. Çünkü dua, kulun özünü ve gönlünü Allah’a yöneltmesidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r3.claim: Believers' salāt for the Prophet means praying for him and remembering him with praise and goodness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r3.anchor: Müminlerin Hz. Peygamber’e salâtı, ona dua etmeleri, onu övgü ve hayırla anmalarıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r4.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r4.claim: When asked how to perform salāt for him, the Prophet taught the salawāt recited in the sitting portions of prayer and said this is how to pray for him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r4.anchor: Resûlullah namazların oturuşlarında okuduğumuz “salavât-ı şerife”yi öğretmiş, “Bana böyle salât edersiniz” demiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r5.claim: Sound sources explain the angels' salāt as supplication, praise, and congratulation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r5.anchor: Sahih kaynaklarda meleklerin salâtı da dua, övgü ve tebrik olarak açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r6.claim: God's salāt upon a servant is a great favor, honor, grace, and mercy, but its nature cannot be known.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r6.anchor: Allah’ın bir kuluna salâtı şüphe yok ki büyük bir iltifat, şeref, lutuf ve rahmettir. Ancak bunun mahiyet ve keyfiyetini bilmek mümkün değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r7.claim: In this usage, sources define God's salāt as mercy and praise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r7.anchor: Kaynaklarda bu açıdan salât, “rahmet ve övgü” şeklinde tanımlanmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r8.claim: Verse 43 calls God's merciful favors to believers and the angels' prayers for them salāt, then states its result: bringing people from darkness into light.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r8.anchor: 43. âyette Allah’ın müminlere rahmetiyle lutuflarda bulunması, meleklerin de onlara dua etmeleri salât kelimesiyle ifade edilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r9.claim: God's salāt is more than praise and mercy: it manifests by opening the eyes and hearts of its recipients to truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r9.anchor: Allah’ın salâtı yalnızca övgü ve rahmetle sınırlı değildir, ona mazhar olanların gözlerini ve gönüllerini hakikate açan bir tecellidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r10.claim: The command to send salāt and salām upon the Prophet is binding, though the verse does not specify its timing, place, or number, leading jurists to differ.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r10.anchor: “Siz de ona salât ve selâm okuyunuz” emri bağlayıcıdır, emrin yerine getirilmesi gereklidir. Ancak bunun zamanı, mekânı ve sayısı konusunda açıklama yapılmadığı için fıkıhçılar farklı yorumlar yapmışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r11.claim: Jurists agree that a person must send salāt and salām upon the Prophet at least once in a lifetime; repeating it at suitable intervals whenever his name is mentioned is recommended.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r11.anchor: Ömürde bir defa Hz. Peygamber’e salavat okumanın ve selâm vermenin farz olduğunda ittifak vardır. Onun adı anıldıkça uygun aralıklarda aynı şeyi yapmanın müstehap

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r12.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r12.claim: Ibn Ashur found no evidence that the Companions recited or wrote salāt each time the Prophet's name appeared; they did so when discussing some of his acts and qualities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r12.anchor: İbn Âşûr yaptığı araştırma sonunda sahâbenin, Hz. Peygamber’in ismi her anıldığında veya yazıldığında salavatı da okuyup yazdıklarına dair bir bilgi bulamadığını kaydetmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r13.claim: The custom of placing salāt at the start of books began under Hārūn al-Rashīd in 181 AH; reciting or writing it at every mention of the Prophet's name became customary later, probably among hadith scholars in the fourth Islamic century.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r13.anchor: Kitapların başlangıcında salavata yer verme (salvele) âdeti Hârûnürreşîd zamanında hicrî 181 yılında başlamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r14.claim: Early Sunni authorities treated salāt for the Prophet and salām offered to him or other prophets in absentia as proper etiquette, while face-to-face salām is for all believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:56/r14.anchor: Ehl-i sünnet’in ilk temsilcileri salavatın Hz. Peygamber’e, kişinin gıyabında selâm vermenin ona ve diğer peygamberlere mahsus olmasını, yüz yüze selâmın bütün müminlere verileceğini bir edep olarak kabul etmişlerdir

BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.claim: The author classifies coordination with God, the Messenger, and believers as a mode of magnification, alongside other pairings of God with the Messenger, angels, or people of knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي

BURHAN:v3p221/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p221/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p221/r4.claim: God's and the angels' prayers have distinct senses, but the author prefers a shared core meaning: care and glorification.
BURHAN:v3p221/r4.anchor: فإن الصلاة من الله مغايرة للصلاة من الملائكة والحق أنه من القدر المشترك وهو الاعتناء والتعظيم

BURHAN:v3p255/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p255/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p255/r6.claim: Prayer is placed before greeting because prayer is superior to salām.

BURHAN:v2p391/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p391/r1.speaker: التنوخي
BURHAN:v2p391/r1.claim: Al-Tanukhi describes degrees of emphasis: a plain verbal clause, then stronger particles and nominal forms, with additional particles or an oath when needed.
BURHAN:v2p391/r1.anchor: قال التنوخي في اقصى القرب اذا قصدوا مجرد الخبر اتوا بالجملة الفعلية وان اكدوا فبالاسمية ثم بان

BURHAN:v2p391/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p391/r2.speaker: قالوا
BURHAN:v2p391/r2.claim: The accusative verbal noun can replace repeating the verb, so تسليما intensifies سلموا as though the verb had been said twice.
BURHAN:v2p391/r2.anchor: قالوا وهو عوض عن تكرار الفعل مرتين فقولك ضربت ضربا بمنزلة قولك ضربت ضربت

BURHAN:v2p391/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p391/r3.speaker: ابن الدهان
BURHAN:v2p391/r3.claim: Ibn al-Dahhan says الظنونا is a plural of ظن, referring to different kinds of conjecture, rather than an emphatic verbal noun.
BURHAN:v2p391/r3.anchor: بل هو جمع ظن وجمع لاختلاف انواعه قاله ابن الدهان

BURHAN:v2p391/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p391/r4.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p391/r4.claim: One view is that the verbal noun removes a metaphor from the agent, so ضربا would mean the prince personally struck the thief.
BURHAN:v2p391/r4.anchor: فقيل انه يرفع المجاز عن الفاعل فانك تقول ضرب الامير اللص ولا يكون باشر بل امر به ضربا علم انه باشر

BURHAN:v2p391/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p391/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p391/r5.claim: Al-Zarkashi says the correct account is that the verbal noun removes ambiguity about the event, not its subject: ضربا rules out metaphorical striking, while نفسه or عينه identifies the agent.
BURHAN:v2p391/r5.anchor: والصواب انه انما يرفع الوهم عن الحديث لا عن المحدث عنه

BURHAN:v2p391/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p391/r8.speaker: ابن الدهان
BURHAN:v2p391/r8.claim: Ibn al-Dahhan cites poetry to show that emphatic verbal nouns can accompany figurative usage, so emphasis does not always eliminate metaphor.
BURHAN:v2p391/r8.anchor: قال ابن الدهان ومما يدل على ان التأكيد لايرفع المجاز قول الشاعر

BURHAN:v3p133/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p133/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p133/r1.claim: On the reading that raises ملائكته, the sense is “God sends blessings” and “His angels send blessings”; the first verb is elided by the second, rather than coordinated with it.
BURHAN:v3p133/r1.anchor: في قراءة من رفع ملائكته أي إن الله يصلي فحذف من الأول لدلالة الثاني عليه وليس عطفا عليه

ITQAN:v3p66/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p66/r3.speaker: حميدة بنت أبي يونس
ITQAN:v3p66/r3.claim: Ḥamīda says her father recited from ʿĀʾisha's codex an addition after the command to bless and greet the Prophet: “and those who pray in the first rows”; she says this was before ʿUthmān changed the codices.
ITQAN:v3p66/r3.anchor: قالت قرأ علي أبي وهو ابن ثمانين سنة في مصحف عائشة ( إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي

ITQAN:v2p412/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p412/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p412/r8.claim: God’s and the angels’ ṣalah upon the Prophet means mercy and seeking forgiveness.
ITQAN:v2p412/r8.anchor: 8 والرحمة والاستغفار ﴿ إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي ﴾

SULAMI:v2p150#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ distinguishes the prayers: God’s are mercy, the angels’ elevation, and the community’s following and love.
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليهم قال : الصلاة من الله رحمة ، والصلاة من الله رحمة ، والصلاة من الملائكة رفعة ، ومن الأمة متابعة ومحبة

SULAMI:v2p150#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r2.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī urges reverent prayer upon the Prophet without imagining that one’s prayers discharge his due.
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r2.anchor: حكى عن الواسطي رحمة الله عليه انه قال : صل عليه بالوقار ولا تجعل لها في قلبك مقدار

SULAMI:v2p150#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r3.speaker: عبد الواحد السياري
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Sayyārī explains that the Prophet’s right exceeds what the whole community could repay; praying for him instead draws mercy upon oneself through him.
SULAMI:v2p150#3/r3.anchor: قال : لا تجعل لصلواتك عليه في قلبك مقدار تظن انك تقضي به من حقه شيئا بصلواتك عليه فإنك تقضي به من حق نفسك

ITQAN:v3p178/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r1.claim: The verbal noun in “submit fully” is an emphatic cognate accusative; the source groups it with emphatic accusatives for the sky’s surging and mountains’ movement.

ITQAN:v3p34/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ITQAN:v3p34/r6.claim: Sibawayh says speakers generally place first what matters more to explain and what they care more to explain.
ITQAN:v3p34/r6.anchor: كما قال سيبويه في كتابه كأنهم يقدمون الذي بيانه أهم وهم ببيانه أعنى

ITQAN:v3p34/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r7.speaker: ابن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p34/r7.claim: Ibn al-Saʾigh says fronting has ten specific purposes beyond the general principle of prioritizing what matters.
ITQAN:v3p34/r7.anchor: قال هذه الحكمة إجمالية وأما تفاصيل أسباب التقديم وأسراره

ITQAN:v3p34/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r9.speaker: ابن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p34/r9.claim: The second purpose is glorification: God precedes the Messenger in “God and His angels send blessings,” “God and the Messenger,” and similar pairings.
ITQAN:v3p34/r9.anchor: الثاني التعظيم كقوله ﴿ ومن يطع الله

ITQAN:v3p162/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p162/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p162/r2.claim: An exception requires omission of the first element: with the nominative reading of “His angels,” the plural predicate applies only to the second subject, so the first predicate is elided.
ITQAN:v3p162/r2.anchor: وقد يجب كونه من الأول نحو

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r1.claim: The Prophet says that whoever invokes blessings upon him once will receive ten blessings from God; al-Wahidi cites the report as found in a ṣaḥīḥ collection.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p362/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

AKHFASH:v2p481#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p481#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p481#2/r1.claim: People's ṣalāh for the Prophet is their supplication for him, while God's ṣalāh is the spreading of good mention about him.
AKHFASH:v2p481#2/r1.anchor: وقال {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي ياأيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما} فصلاة الناس عليه دعاؤهم له

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r8.claim: One reported sense is forgiveness: God’s ṣalāt upon the Prophet means forgiveness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r8.anchor: والثاني : المغفرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحزاب :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r1.speaker: لبيد
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r1.claim: Lexically rukūʿ is bending; Labīd’s line uses rākʿ for one who bends when rising.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r1.anchor:
قال لبيد : -
أخبر أخبار القرون التي مضت … أدب كأني كلما قمت راكع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r2.claim: Rukūʿ can mean abasement, illustrated by an anonymous verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r2.anchor: ( 60 / أ ) ويقال : الركوع ، ويراد به : الذل . وأنشدوا من ذلك :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r3.claim: Exegetes use rukūʿ for prayer as a whole; 2:43 means pray with those who pray.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r3.anchor: أحدها : الصلاة بجملتها . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ واركعوا مع الراكعين ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r4.claim: A second sense is physical bowing, as in the command to bow and prostrate.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r4.anchor: والثاني : الانحناء . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج : ﴿ اركعوا واسجدوا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r5.claim: A third sense is prostration, as in David’s falling down and turning back to God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p314/r5.anchor: ( والثالث : السجود ) . ومنه قوله تعالى في ص : ﴿ وخر راكعا وأناب ﴾

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r4.claim: God's الصلاة is mercy and forgiveness, as shown by verses pairing divine prayers with mercy and by God's and the angels' prayers for the Prophet and believers.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r4.speaker: البصريون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r4.claim: The Basrans also allow the construction and cite “Indeed God and His angels bless the Prophet” as an example.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r4.anchor: والبصريون يجيزونه، ويحكون: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r5.claim: An anonymous poem coordinating “Qiyār” with the first-person subject after inna supports the construction.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p38/r5.anchor: وينشدون : فمن يك أمسى بالمدينة رحله

SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r1.claim: The common reading has accusative coordination with اسم إن.
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r1.anchor: العامة على النصب نسقا على اسم " إن ".

SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r2.claim: It is disputed whether يصلون predicates of God and angels or angels alone, with God's predicate omitted because the prayers differ.
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r2.anchor: و " يصلون " هل هو خبر عن الله وملائكته، أو عن الملائكة فقط، وخبر الجلالة محذوف لتغاير الصلاتين؟ خلاف

SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and a report from Abu Amr read the noun nominative, coordinating syntactically or as a new subject with omitted predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:33:56/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ورويت عن أبي عمرو " وملائكته " رفعا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reads فصلوا عليه, introducing the imperative with fāʾ.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن: "يا أيها الذين آمنوا فصلوا عليه2"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r2.claim: The fāʾ makes prayer sound conditionally owed because God has prayed for the Prophet; Ibn Jinnī prefers the common bare imperative صلوا عليه as stronger, since it gives no stated cause inviting an objection.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p183/r2.anchor: دخول الفاء إنما هو لما ضمنه الحديث من معنى الشرط، وذلك أنه إنما وجبت عليه الصلاة منا لأن الله "سبحانه" قد صلى عليه،

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r1.claim: The opening clause explains the preceding extraordinary honor; its nominal opening signals continuity, while its verbal predicate signals renewed prayer over time.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r1.anchor: الجملة تفيد الدوام نظرا إلى صدرها من حيث أنها جملة أسمية وتفيد التجدد نظرا إلى عجزها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r2.claim: The emphatic إن marks the importance of the statement, or answers the implicit question about the cause of this great honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r2.anchor: وتأكيدها بأن للإعتناء بشأن الخبر وقيل لوقوعها في جواب سؤال مقدر هو ما سبب هذا التشريف العظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r3.claim: Calling him the Prophet rather than naming him, contrary to the usual way God recounts His prophets, signals his exceptional dignity; the definite article marks him as the preeminent bearer of the title.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r3.anchor: وعبر بالنبي دون أسمه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على خلاف الغالب في حكايته تعالى عن أنبيائه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r4.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r4.claim: Some eminent scholars say النبي is used instead of الرسول to connect with the preceding رسول الله; since most hold messengership superior to prophethood, attaching prayer to the lower rank underscores his entitlement. Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salam disagrees.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة : إن ذاك للأشعار بعلة الحكم ولم يعبر بالرسول بدله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r5.claim: The annexation in ملائكته conveys comprehensiveness.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r6.claim: Saying His angels highlights their rank; their attribution to God honors the Prophet, and the vast company conveys prayer reaching him continuously through the ages.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : ( ملائكته ) ولم يقل الملائكة إشارة إلى عظيم قدرهم ومزيد شرفهم بإضافتهم إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r7.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya explains God's prayer as His praise and exaltation of the Prophet before the angels; al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas also transmits this explanation, which al-Halimi adopts.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r7.anchor: هي منه عزوجل ثناؤه عليه عند ملائكته وتعظيمه ورواه البخاري عن أبي العالية وغيره عن الربيع بن أنس

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r8.claim: This exaltation appears in the world by raising his mention, manifesting his religion and preserving his law, and in the afterlife through intercession, reward, the Praised Station and precedence among the honored.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r8.anchor: تعظيمه تعالى إياه في الدنيا بإعلاء ذكره وإظهار دينه وإبقاء العمل بشريعته وفي الآخرة بتشفيعه في أمته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r9.claim: The angels' prayer means their supplication for the Prophet, according to Abu al-ʿAliya as transmitted by ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r9.anchor: وهي من الملائكة الدعاء له عليه الصلاة والسلام على ما رواه عبد بن حميد وإبن أبي حاتم عن أبي العالية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r10.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation makes God's prayer His mercy; al-Thawri and other scholars, Abu al-ʿAliya and al-Dahhak transmit it, and al-Mawardi calls it the most apparent explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p75#2/r10.anchor: هي منه تعالى رحمته عزوجل ونقله الترمذي عن الثوري وغير واحد من أهل العلم ونقل عن أبي العالية أيضا وعن الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r1.claim: The objection to understanding God's prayer as mercy refers back to the discussion of 33:43, هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته; the same answer applies.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ) والجواب هو الجواب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r2.claim: The Companions' question about how to pray for the Prophet suggests they distinguished prayer from ordinary mercy, since they already knew how to ask for mercy in the tashahhud.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r2.anchor: بأن الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم سألوا كما سيأتي قريبا إن شاء الله تعالى لما نزلت عن كيفية الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r3.speaker: author
