ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r3.claim: A response says the prayer is a particular mercy, so they asked how to obtain that specific kind; this makes the word carry two meanings for God and the angels, which many Hanafis and others reject.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r3.anchor: وأجيب بأنها رحمة خاصة فسألوا عن الكيفية ليحيطوا علما بذلك الخصوص وهي من الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r4.claim: One solution to the two-meanings objection posits ellipsis: God prays and the angels pray, with a separate verb suited to each meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم : في الآية حذف والأصل إن الله يصلي وملائكته يصلون فيكون قد أدى كل معنى بلفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r5.claim: Another reply is that having multiple agents makes the verb function as though it were multiple verbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r5.anchor: وقال آخر : تعدد الفاعل صير الفعل كالمتعدد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r6.speaker: صدر الشريعة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r6.claim: Sadr al-Shariʿa proposes one literal meaning, supplication for good: God directs Himself and the angels to convey good, which means mercy for God and seeking forgiveness for angels; al-Alusi finds this doubtful.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r6.anchor: وقال صدر الشريعة يجوز أن يكون المعنى واحدا حقيقا وهو الدعاء والمعنى والله تعالى أعلم أنه تعالى يدعو ذاته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r7.speaker: جمع من المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r7.claim: A group of careful scholars avoids equivocation through a general metaphor: care for the Prophet's good and welfare, disclosure of his honor and magnification, or spiritual compassion.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r7.anchor: وقال جمع من المحققين : يتقصى عن ذلك بعموم المجاز فيراد معنى مجازي عام يكون كل من المعاني فردا حقيقيا له

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r8.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r8.claim: Some eminent scholars say the meaning of prayer changes according to the state of the one praying, the recipient of prayer, and the one prayed for.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r8.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة : إن معنى الصلاة يختلف بإعتبار حال المصلي والمصلي له والمصلي عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r9.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r9.claim: Another view says prayer has one linguistic sense, inclination or favor (عطف): mercy for God, seeking forgiveness for angels, and supplication for people; critics object that literal inclination cannot be predicated of God, while its defenders distinguish unseen divine reality from bodily human experience.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p76/r9.anchor: وقال آخر : الصواب أن الصلاة لغة بمعنى واحد وهو العطف ثم هو بالنسبة إليه تعالى الرحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r1.claim: The Salaf did not reinterpret divine mercy through the two familiar figurative explanations; requiring such interpretation would leave very little scripture without it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r1.anchor: وقد ذهب السلف إلى عدم تأويل الرحمة فيه تعالى بأحد التأويلين المشهورين مع أنها في الشاهد لا تتحقق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r2.claim: Al-Alusi favors prayer here as honoring the Prophet, with an inclination appropriate to God and the angels; when applied to believers, it means what suits each of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r2.anchor: وقد يختار أن الصلاة هنا تعظيم لشأنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقارنه عطف لائق به تعالى وبملائكته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r3.claim: Combining God and angels under one pronoun can honor the angels without implying any deficiency in God.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r3.anchor: وجمع الله سبحانه والملائكة في ضمير واحد لا ينافي قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لمن قال

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r4.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r4.claim: The Prophet rebuked a preacher who said whoever obeys God and His Messenger has prospered and whoever disobeys them has strayed, telling him to repeat Allah and His Messenger separately.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r4.anchor: بئس خطيب القوم أنت قل ومن يعص الله ورسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r5.claim: Some say combining the two is generally unobjectionable; the preacher was censured for pausing after يعصهما, and they cite a report in Abu Dawud.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا بأس بذلك مطلقا وذم الخطيب لأنه وقف على يعصهما

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r6.claim: Another view calls the combined pronoun objectionable across two clauses but acceptable in one clause, as here and in the Prophet's speech; al-Alusi says this needs examination.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r6.anchor: وقيل يقبح إذا كان في جملتين كما في كلام الخطيب ولا يقبح إذا كان في واحدة كما في الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعبدالوارث عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAbd al-Warith from Abu ʿAmr read ملائكته in the nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r7.anchor: وقرأ إبن عباس وعبدالوارث عن أبي عمرو ( وملائكته ) بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r8.speaker: الكوفيون غير الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r8.claim: The Kufans other than al-Farraʾ construe the nominative as coordinated with the syntactic position of إن and its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r8.anchor: فعند الكوفيين غير الفراء هو عطف على محل أن وأسمها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r9.claim: Al-Farraʾ permits coordination with إن's subject when its case ending is hidden, as in 2:62 and the cited verse of poetry; grammarians differ whether this covers a noun ending in a long vowel or one annexed to ياء.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r9.anchor: والفراء يشترط في العطف على ذلك خفاء إعراب أسم إن كما في قوله تعالى ( إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r10.speaker: البصريون والفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r10.claim: The Basrans and al-Farraʾ instead parse ملائكته as a subject whose predicate is يصلون, with إن's predicate omitted because the following clause makes it clear: God prays and His angels pray.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r10.anchor: وعند البصريين والفراء هو مبتدأ وجملة ( يصلون ) خبره وخبر إن محذوف ثقة بدلالة ما بعد عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r11.claim: The command calls believers to honor the Prophet in keeping with the honor God and the angels give him; its surface wording does not explicitly command imitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r11.anchor: أي عظموا شأنه عاطفين عليه فإنكم أولى بذلك وظاهر سوق الآية أنه لا يجاب إقتدائنا به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading صلوا عليه كما صلى عليه and al-Hasan's فصلوا عليه make the preceding interpretation clearer and weaken the claim that the command means simply to say a fixed invocation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77/r12.anchor: قراءة إبن مسعود صلوا عليه كما صلى عليه وكذا قراءة الحسن فصلوا عليه أظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r1.claim: Those who gloss the command as saying اللهم صل على النبي mean that this wording, or a similar invocation asking God to honor him, is the commanded form because believers cannot fulfill his due honor themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r1.anchor: ومن فسره بذلك أراد أن المراد بالتعظيم المأمور به ما يكون بهذا اللفظ ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r2.claim: The transmitted formulas guide believers to the manner and form of prayer; they do not define the lexical meaning of صلوا, and their several forms may be combined.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r2.anchor: وما جاء في الأخبار إرشاد إلى كيفية ذلك وصفته لا أنه تفسير للفظ صلوا وجاء ذلك على عدة أوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r3.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r3.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports that a man asked how to pray for the Prophet after learning the greeting; the Prophet taught asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham's family, and to bless them. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r3.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رجل : يارسول الله أما السلام عليك فقد علمناه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r4.speaker: أبو حميد الساعدي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r4.claim: Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi reports that the Prophet taught praying for Muhammad, his wives and descendants as for Abraham's family, and asking blessing for them likewise. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي حميد الساعدي أنهم قالوا : يارسول الله كيف نصلي عليك فقال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports that the Prophet taught asking God to pray upon His servant and messenger as upon Abraham and to bless Muhammad and his family as Abraham. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p77#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قلنا : يارسول الله هذا السلام عليك قد علمنا فكيف الصلاة عليك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet taught asking God to pray upon and bless Muhammad and his family as He did Abraham and his family throughout the worlds, ending with حميد مجيد; the greeting was already known. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة إنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف نصلي عليك قال : قولوا اللهم صل على محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r2.speaker: ابن بريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r2.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Prophet taught asking God to place His prayers, mercy and blessings upon Muhammad and his family as He placed them upon Abraham. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r2.anchor: عن إبن بريدة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قلنا يارسول الله قد علمنا كيف نسلم عليك فكيف نصلي عليك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r3.claim: Al-Alusi notes that some of the cited reports have been criticized, without specifying which ones here.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r3.anchor: إلى غير ذلك مما ملئت منه كتب الحديث إلا أن في بعض الروايات المذكورة فيها مقالا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r4.speaker: الباجي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r4.claim: The apparent question asks for the form or manner of prayer, as al-Baji prefers and al-Qurtubi states definitively; an alternative says they asked its meaning and wording because they expected a fixed liturgical formula and sought textual instruction rather than analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r4.anchor: والظاهر من السؤال أنه سؤال عن الصفة كما أشرنا إليه قبل وهو الذي رجحه الباجي وغيره وجزم به القرطبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r5.claim: Al-Alusi favors the manner-of-prayer reading: after learning of God's and the angels' honoring, the Companions did not know which form of honor suited them, so the Prophet directed them to its best form and to ask God for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78/r5.anchor: لما سمعوا الأمر بالصلاة بعد سماع أن الله عزوجل وملائكته عليهم السلام يصلون عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r1.claim: Asking God to pray upon the Prophet is the greatest form of honor because it acknowledges believers' inability to give him the honor he deserves.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r1.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم أن الآتي بما أمر به من طلب الصلاة له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عزوجل آت بأعظم أنواع التعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r2.claim: The saying attributed to Abu Bakr, the Siddiq, that inability to comprehend comprehension is itself comprehension roughly parallels this point.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r2.anchor: وقد قيل ونسب إلى الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه العجز عن درك الأدراك إدراك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r3.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r3.claim: A view transmitted and approved by Abu al-Yumn ibn ʿAsakir says believers delegate the prayer to God because He knows its due form and His intention; al-Alusi says his own formulation is subtler.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r3.anchor: قول بعض الأجلة ونقله أبو اليمن بن عساكر وحسنه لما أمرنا الله تعالى بالصلاة على نبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r4.claim: The apparent direction of the Prophet's instruction requires asking God to pray for him; اللهم صل على محمد suffices because all the reported forms agree on it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r4.anchor: أنه لا يحصل إمتثال الأمر إلا بما فيه طلب ذلك منه عزوجل ويكفي اللهم صل على محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r5.claim: Among those who require prayer upon the Prophet within ritual prayer, the stronger view accepts صلى الله على محمد, while الصلاة على رسول الله does not suffice by agreement because it does not attribute the prayer to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r5.anchor: يكفي صلى الله على محمد على الأصح بخلاف الصلاة على رسول الله فإنه لا يجزي إتفاقا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r6.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r6.claim: Ibn Hajar's Tuhfa says الصلاة على محمد apparently suffices if intended as supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r6.anchor: وفي تحفة إبن حجر يكفي الصلاة على محمد إن نوى بها الدعاء فيما يظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r7.speaker: النيسابوري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r7.claim: Al-Nishaburi says صليت على محمد is insufficient: the servant should ask his Lord to pray for the Prophet, so God is the actual agent and the servant is only figuratively praying.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r7.anchor: وقال النيسابوري : لا يكفي صليت على محمد لأن مرتبة العبد تقصر عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r8.claim: The request form is considered better than the declarative form. The suggestion that hadith scholars use declaratives to avoid confusing lay listeners about whether God's prayer has occurred is weak; Al-Alusi prefers avoiding interruption and mixed styles in flowing prose.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p78#2/r8.anchor: وذكروا أن الإتيان بصيغة الطلب أفضل من الإتيان بصيغة الخبر وأجيب عن إطباق المحدثين على الإتيان بها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r1.claim: The command is not fulfilled by asking God merely to exalt Muhammad in suitably honoring terms without a word derived from prayer; the majority understand both commands as prescribed formulas, including اللهم صل على النبي and السلام عليك أيها النبي.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r1.anchor: والظاهر أنه لا يحصل الإمتثال باللهم عظم محمدا التعظيم اللائق ونحوه مما ليس فيه مشتق من الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r2.claim: The first and strongest reading of السلام عليك is a prayer for the Prophet's safety from defects and harms, with السلام as a verbal noun meaning safety; على is used for praise rather than a sense of decree or dominion.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r2.anchor: والأرجح عندي هو الوجه الأول وقيل : معنى ( سلموا تسليما )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r3.speaker: ابن فورك
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r3.claim: A second interpretation takes السلام as God's name and the phrase as His ongoing care and guardianship; Ibn Furak and others define the name as the possessor of safety from every defect in essence, attribute and act.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r3.anchor: ويكون السلام هنا أسم الله تعالى ومعناه على ما أختاره إبن فورك وغيره من عدة أقوال ذو السلامة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r4.claim: On the divine-name reading, another explanation means that the Prophet be granted goodness and blessing and protected from harm, since invoking God's name upon something confers that benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r4.anchor: وقيل : إذا أريد بالسلام ما هو من أسمائه تعالى فالمراد لا خلوت من الخير والبركة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r5.claim: A further explanation supplies an omitted word: حفظ الله عليك, a prayer that God preserve the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r5.anchor: وقيل : الكلام على هذا التقدير على حذف المضاف أي حفظ الله تعالى عليك والمراد الدعاء بالحفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r6.claim: A third interpretation takes salām as peace or non-opposition and asks God to make people submit to the Prophet and his law; على suits the turning toward someone in obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r6.anchor: وثالثها الإنقياد عليك على أن السلام من المسالمة وعدم المخالفة والمراد الدعاء بأن يصير الله تعالى العباد منقادين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says the command may mean obedience to the Prophet's orders, but the apparent reports and traditions support the greeting or prayer for safety, which most scholars adopt.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r7.anchor: وقيل : معنى ( سلموا تسليما ) إنقادوا لأوامره صلى الله عليه وسلم إنقيادا وهو غير بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r8.claim: The sentence is declarative in form but functions as a supplication asking God to grant the Prophet safety.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r8.anchor: والجملة صيغة خبر معناها الدعاء بالسلامة وطلبها منه تعالى لنبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r9.claim: Some raise a theological problem: supplication entails distinct requester, requested object and recipient; if God asks another for the Prophet's safety it is impossible, while asking Himself seems to require self-distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p79/r9.anchor: وأستشكل ذلك فيما إذا قال الله تعالى السلام عليك أيها النبي أو نحوه بأن الدعاء لا يتصور منه عزوجل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r1.claim: The reply says one may request or will something of oneself just as one may will it of another; humans command and prohibit themselves, as scripture states, and God's request can more clearly be understood as His will.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r1.anchor: قال سبحانه ( إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r2.claim: Explanations of اللهم سلم على النبي include: God, say peace upon him; God, bring or realize safety for him; and God, protect him from defects and harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r2.anchor: ومعنى اللهم سلم على النبي اللهم قل السلام على النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r3.speaker: بعض المعاصرين
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r3.claim: A contemporary scholar treats God's السلام عليك as performative speech that creates safety, by analogy with contract formulas; Al-Alusi prefers the direct sense of bringing safety rather than saying the greeting, to reduce mediation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المعاصرين : إن السلام عليك ونحوه من الله عزوجل لإنشاء السلامة وإيجادها بهذا اللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r4.claim: God's greeting of prophets means He has made them recipients of invocation and praise, as in His greetings to Noah, Abraham, Moses and Aaron.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r4.anchor: وقد يكون السلام منه عزوجل على أنبيائه عليهم السلام نحو قوله سبحانه ( سلام على نوح في العالمين سلام على إبراهيم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r5.claim: تسليما is an emphatic verbal noun; salām is explicitly emphasized because God's and the angels' prayer already assures the prayer, whereas salām has no such confirming context.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80/r5.anchor: ونصب ( تسليما ) على أنه مصدر مؤكد وأكد سبحانه التسليم ولم يؤكد الصلاة قيل لأنها مؤكدة بإعلامه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r1.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim explains that prayer is already emphatic through إن and the universal جمع for angels, urging immediate imitation; salām lacks that emphasis, so its verbal noun reinforces the bare command. Both prayers and greetings are repeated as report and request, and salām's later position makes emphasis useful.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r1.anchor: وإلى هذا يؤل قول إبن القيم التأكيد فيهما وإن أختلف جهته فإنه تعالى أخبر في الأول بصلاته وصلاة ملائكته عليه مؤكدا له

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r2.claim: An ellipsis analysis reconstructs صلوا عليه تصلية وسلموا عليه تسليما, omitting عليه from one clause and the verbal noun from the other; prayer is attributed to God and angels while believers are ordered to do both.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن في الكلام الإحتباك والأصل صلوا عليه تصلية وسلموا عليه تسليما فحذف عليه من إحدى الجملتين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r3.claim: One explanation says God's and the angels' prayer includes greeting, while believers must also obey and submit; because their prayer need not include submission, they are explicitly commanded to greet and obey.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : الصلاة من الله سبحانه والملائكة متضمنة للسلام بمعنى التحية الذي لا يتصور غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi finds the second explanation stronger: prayer by God and angels entails greeting, but believers must explicitly be told to submit, since their prayer does not entail both senses; he notes a difficulty in its argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p80#2/r4.anchor: ثم قيل : وهذا أولى مما قبله لأن ذلك يرد عليه قوله تعالى : ( سلام على إبراهيم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r1.speaker: الشهاب الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r1.claim: Al-Shihab al-Khafaji sees a subtle reason for the omission of divine and angelic salām and its emphasis for believers: the preceding passage discusses harm to the Prophet, which people inflict, and salām asks that he be kept safe from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r1.anchor: وقال الشهاب الخفاجي عليه الرحمة : قد لاح لي في ترك تأكيد السلام وتخصيصه بالمؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r2.claim: A tentative explanation says the believers already knew God's and the angels' greeting and the form of their own greeting; the verse's prayer statement could otherwise imply that salām was unimportant or its request abrogated, so it is commanded emphatically.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r2.anchor: وربما يقال على بعد في ذلك : إنه يمكن أن يكون سلام الله تعالى وملائكته عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام معلوما

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r3.claim: Most scholars treat the imperative as obligatory; some claim consensus. Al-Tabari's claim that it is recommended by consensus is rejected or construed as recommending more than the once-in-a-lifetime minimum, which al-Qurtubi says is undisputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r3.anchor: والأمر في الآية عند الأكثرين للوجوب بل ذكر بعضهم إجماع الأئمة والعلماء عليه ودعوى محمد بن جرير الطبري أنه للندب بالإجماع مردودة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r4.claim: The majority, including Abu Hanifa and Malik, require prayer once in a lifetime: the unrestricted command does not require repetition, and one performance fulfills the act.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r4.anchor: قيل : واجبة مرة في العمر ككلمة التوحيد لأن الأمر مطلق لا يقتضي تكرارا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r5.claim: Other legal positions require prayer in every tashahhud or in every ritual prayer; a minority of Hanbalis make it a designated opening invocation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81/r5.anchor: وقيل : واجبة في التشهد مطلقا وقيل : واجبة في مصلق الصلاة وتفرد بعض الحنابلة بتعين دعاء الإفتتاح بها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن بكير
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r1.claim: A position attributed to Qadi Abu Bakr ibn Bukayr requires frequent prayer without setting a number.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r1.anchor: وقيل : يجب الإكثار منها من غير تعيين بعدد وحكى ذلك عن القاضي أبي بكر بن بكير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r2.claim: Other positions require prayer once at each gathering, in every supplication, or each time the Prophet is mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : تجب في كل مجلس مرة وإن تكرر ذكره صلى الله عليه وسلم مرارا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r3.speaker: الطحاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r3.claim: The view requiring prayer at every mention is held by groups of Hanafis, Shafiʿis, Malikis and some Hanbalis; al-Tahawi says it is due whenever one hears the Prophet mentioned or mentions him oneself.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r3.anchor: وبه قال جمع من الحنفية منهم الطحاوي وعبارته تجب كلما سمع ذكره من غيره أو ذكره بنفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r4.claim: Proponents cite reports threatening humiliation, distance, misery, miserliness and rudeness for neglecting prayer; most regard these threats as signs of obligation, though the view was also linked to the weak rule that unrestricted commands imply repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r4.anchor: قيل وهو مبني على القول الضعيف في الأصول أن الأمر المطلق يفيد التكرار وليس كذلك بل له أدلة أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r5.claim: Critics say the every-mention duty contradicts prior consensus, since no Companion or Successor is known to have held it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r5.anchor: وأعترض هذا القول كثيرون بأنه مخالف للأجماع المنعقد قبل قائله إذ لم يعرف عن صحابي ولا تابعي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r6.claim: Critics argue the rule would prevent other worship and burden callers to prayer, listeners, reciters passing over the Prophet's name, and those uttering the two testimonies, contrary to the law's ease.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r6.anchor: وبأنه يلزم على عمومه أن لا يتفرغ السامع لعبادة أخرى وأنها تجب على المؤذن وسامعه والقاريء المار بذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r7.claim: Critics add that praising God whenever He is mentioned would be more deserving of obligation, yet proponents do not require it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r7.anchor: وبأن الثناء على الله تعالى كلما ذكر أحق بالوجوب ولم يقولوا به

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r8.claim: Critics note that no report preserves a Companion saying to the Prophet, may God pray upon you.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r8.anchor: وبأنه لا يحفظ عن صحابي أنه قال : يارسول الله صلى الله عليك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r9.claim: Critics answer that the warning reports are rhetorical exaggeration emphasizing the duty's importance, particularly for someone habitually neglecting prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p81#2/r9.anchor: وبأن تلك الأحاديث المحتج بها للوجوب خرجت مخرج المبالغة في تأكد ذلك وطلبه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r1.claim: It is not enough to refute those who require the blessing by noting that no Companion or Successor report against obligation was preserved; one would need an explicit transmitted consensus of non-obligation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r1.anchor: فكيف يسعهم خرق الإجماع على أنه لا يكفي في الرد عليهم كونه لم يحفظ عن صحابي أو تابعي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r2.claim: The objection that performing the blessing leaves no time for other worship is denied: one can devote time to other acts of worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r2.anchor: وأما الثاني فممنوع بل يمكن التفرغ لعبادات أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r3.claim: The proponents of obligation can accept the third objection's consequence; the author says it entails no hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r3.anchor: فللقائلين بالوجوب إلتزامه وليس فيه حرج

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r4.claim: Some scholars explicitly state that the obligation also applies with respect to God, answering the fourth objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r4.anchor: فلأن جمعا صرحوا بالوجوب في حقه تعالى أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r5.claim: Several routes from Companions report that when they addressed the Prophet, they said, May God bless you.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r5.anchor: ورد في عدة طرق عن عدة من الصحابة أنهم لما قالوا : يارسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r6.claim: The sixth objection cannot be answered by interpreting the hadiths as proposed without supplying the supporting chain of evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r6.anchor: حمل الأحاديث على ما ذكر لا يكفي إلا مع بيان سنده ولم يبينوه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r7.claim: Those requiring the blessing differ: most make it an individual duty for every person, while some regard it as a communal duty.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r7.anchor: أكثرهم على أن ذلك فرض عين على كل فرد فرد وبعضهم على أنه فرض كفاية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r8.speaker: صاحب المجتبى
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r8.claim: Whether the duty recurs with every mention of the Prophet in one gathering is disputed: one commentary says once suffices as the sound view, while the Mujtaba says it recurs.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r8.anchor: وفي بعض شروح الهداية يكفي مرة على الصحيح وقال صاحب المجتبي : يتكرر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r9.claim: The blessing is not repeated with each mention of God; a proposed distinction is that divine rights allow leniency while human rights are strict, but calling this God's right merely because He commanded it misunderstands the intended category.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r9.anchor: وفي تكرر ذكر الله تعالى لا يتكرر وفرق هو وغيره بينهما بما فيه نظر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r10.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r10.claim: Al-Shafi'i's established position requires the blessing in the final sitting of prayer, between tashahhud and the concluding salutation; al-Asnawi transmits another view calling it a sunna, which leading Shafi'i scholars did not adopt.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r10.anchor: وقيل : إنها تجب في القعود آخر الصلاة بين التشهد وسلام التحلل وهذا هو مذهب الشافعي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r11.claim: Ibn Masud authentically said that after tashahhud in prayer, a person blesses the Prophet and then makes personal supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r11.anchor: فقد صح عنه أنه قال : يتشهد الرجل في الصلاة ثم يصلي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r12.speaker: أبو مسعود البدري وابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r12.claim: Abu Masud al-Badri and Ibn Umar authentically say a prayer includes recitation, tashahhud, and blessing on the Prophet; omission of any calls for two prostrations after the salutation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r12.anchor: فقد صح عنهما أنه لا تكون صلاة إلا بقراءة وتشهد وصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r13.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r13.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says they taught tashahhud, then praise and glorification of God, blessing on the Prophet, and finally asking one's need.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82/r13.anchor: الشعبي فقد صح عنه كنا نعلم التشهد فإذا قال : وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from al-Shaʿbi that one who omits blessing on the Prophet in tashahhud must repeat the prayer, or else that the prayer does not suffice.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عنه من لم يصل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في التشهد فليعد صلاته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.speaker: محمد الباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi relates a similar view from Muhammad al-Baqir, which al-Daraqutni judged sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r2.anchor: والإمام أبو جعفر محمد الباقر فقد روى البيهقي عنه نحو ما ذكر عن الشعبي وصوبه الدارقطني

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.claim: Ibn Hajar says he found no Companion or Successor explicitly denying obligation except Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, suggesting the others held it obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r3.anchor: لم أر عن أحد من الصحابة والتابعين التصريح بعدم الوجوب إلا ما نقل عن إبراهيم النخعي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.claim: Ahmad has two transmitted positions, and the author considers the later report to be obligation: Ahmad said he had hesitated but then concluded the blessing was obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.anchor: فإنه قال : كنت أتهيب ذلك ثم تبينت فإذا الصلاة على النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.claim: In Ishaq ibn Rahwayh's later report, deliberately omitting the blessing invalidates prayer, while for forgetful omission he hopes the prayer suffices; this is also a Malikite position chosen by Ibn al-Arabi.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r5.anchor: إذا تركها عمدا بطلت صلاته أو سهوا رجوت أن تجزئة وهو قول عند المالكية أختاره إبن العربي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.claim: Requiring blessing at every mention would entail it in tashahhud, but requiring it there does not make it a condition of prayer's validity; this evidence rebuts the claim that al-Shafiʿi innovated by requiring it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r6.anchor: إلا أنه يرد على القائلين بأن الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه شذ في قوله بالوجوب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi's argument is set out in al-Umm; his followers defend it with hadiths of differing strength and wrote treatises answering critics including Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Khattabi, and al-Tahawi.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r7.anchor: وأما دليله رضي الله تعالى عنه على ذلك فمذكور في الأم وقد استدل له أصحابه بعدة أحاديث

ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.claim: The author condemns attacking an imam like al-Shafiʿi and calls partisanship without adequate investigation reprehensible; the discussion of salutation follows the same debate as that of blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p82#2/r8.anchor: وأنا أرى التشنيع على مثل هذا الإمام شنيعا والتعصب مع قلة التتبع أمرا فظيعا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r1.claim: Ibn Faris says blessing and salutation share the same obligatory status because both are commanded in the verse, and a command denotes obligation unless evidence redirects it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r1.anchor: صرح ابن فارس اللغوي بأنهما سيان في الفرضية لأن كلا منهما مأمور به في الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r2.claim: The best formula is the one the Prophet taught his Companions when they asked, since he would choose the finest form for himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r2.anchor: وأفضل الكيفيات في الصلاة عليه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ما علمه رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام لأصحابه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r3.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r3.claim: Al-Nawawi says in al-Rawda that someone who vows to bless the Prophet in the best manner fulfills the vow only with the Prophetic formula taught to the Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r3.anchor: قال النووي في الروضة : لو حلف ليصلين على النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r4.speaker: السبكي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r4.claim: Al-Subki explains that this formula certainly performs the requested blessing and brings the reward mentioned in hadiths for that form.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r4.anchor: ووجهه السبكي بأن من أتى بها فقد صلى الصلاة المطلوبة بيقين وكان له الخير الوارد في أحاديث الصلاة كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r5.speaker: المروزي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r5.claim: Al-Marwazi holds that a person fulfills the vow with the formula asking blessings on Muhammad and his family whenever those who remember remember and those who forget overlook.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r5.anchor: ونقل الرافعي عن المروزي أنه يبر باللهم صل على محمد وآل محمد كلما ذكرك الذاكرون

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r6.speaker: القاضي حسين
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r6.claim: Qadi Husayn's proposed vow-fulfilling formula is, O God, bless Muhammad as befits and is due to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي حسين : طريق البر اللهم صل على محمد كما هو أهله ومستحقه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r7.speaker: البارزي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r7.claim: Al-Barizi prefers a formula asking God for the best blessings on Muhammad and his family, in a number equal to God's known things.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r7.anchor: واختار البارزي أن الأفضل اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد أفضل صلواتك وعدد معلوماتك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r8.speaker: الكمال بن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r8.claim: Kamal ibn al-Humam says all mentioned formulas are contained in an expansive prayer asking God's finest blessings, honor, and nearness for the Prophet and his family.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r8.anchor: وقال الكمال بن الهمام : كلما ذكر من الكيفيات موجود في اللهم صل أبدا أفضل صلواتك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r9.speaker: ابن حجر الهيثمي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r9.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami selects yet another formula as the best, without its wording being specified here.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r9.anchor: واختار ابن حجر الهيثمي غير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r10.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r10.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam, as transmitted by Ibn Arafa, requires an added taslīm in the salutation wording; al-Alusi says that appeal to the verse's surface wording is unsound on reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r10.anchor: ونقل ابن عرفة عن ابن عبدالسلام أنه لا بد في السلام عليه صل الله تعالى عليه وسلم أن يزيد تسليما

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r11.claim: A group of Companions and later authorities held that blessing is not confined to transmitted formulas if an eloquent wording clearly expresses the Prophet's honor and high status.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r11.anchor: ونقل عن جمع من الصحابة ومن بعدهم أن كيفية الصلاة عليه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لا يوقف فيها مع المنصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r12.claim: Ibn Masud advises making the blessing beautiful because it may be presented to the Prophet; when asked for wording, he gives a long invocation for blessings, mercy, and the Prophet's praiseworthy station, ending with the Abrahamic formula.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r12.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : إذا صليتم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأحسنوا الصلاة عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r13.claim: The wording subtly signals that blessing should be rendered beautifully: the phrase can form a hemistich of the kāmil meter, a subtle point the author regards as valuable.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r13.anchor: رمز خفي فيما أرى إلى مطلوبية تحسين الصلاة عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام حيث أتى به كلاما يصلح أن يكون شطرا من البحر الكامل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r14.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r14.claim: Al-Nawawi and some others infer that separating blessing from salutation is disliked because the verse commands both together; critics cite teaching reports in which salutation came first, but the response is that the order was incidental, not deliberate separation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r14.anchor: واستدل النووي رحمه الله تعالى بالآية على كراهة إفراد الصلاة عن السلام وعكسه لورود الأمر بهما معا فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r15.speaker: ابن حجر الهيثمي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r15.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami says the intended dislike is only خلاف الأولى, since no specific evidence establishing the cause for a stronger prohibition exists.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83/r15.anchor: وذكر العلامة ابن حجر الهيثمي أن الحق أن المراد بالكراهة خلاف الأولى إذ لم يوجد مقتضيها من النهي المخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r1.speaker: الحموي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r1.claim: Al-Hamawi transmits from Minyat al-Mufti that Hanafis do not consider separating either blessing or salutation disliked; Mirak says this disagreement concerns the Prophet, while other prophets may be addressed separately without dislike.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r1.anchor: ونقل الحموي من أصحابنا عن منية المفتي أنه لا يكره عندنا أفراد أحدهما عن الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r2.claim: Some restrict the dislike to separating the phrases in speech, not in writing, as occurs in al-Umm.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r2.anchor: وصرح بعضهم أن الكراهة عند من يقول بها إنما هي في الأفراد لفظا وأما الأفراد خطا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r3.claim: The author finds the verse a very weak proof for disliking separation: it commands blessing and salutation absolutely, without requiring them at the same time; one could bless in the morning and salute in the evening and fulfill the commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r3.anchor: إذ قصارى ما تدل عليه أن كلا من الصلاة والتسليم مأمور به مطلقا ولا تدل على الأمر بالإتيان بهما في زمان واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r4.claim: Although the verse does not require simultaneous pairing, most early Muslims combined the two; the author dislikes abandoning that practice, which also avoids an unlikely irreverent misunderstanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r4.anchor: نعم درج أكثر السلف على الجمع بينهما فلا أستحسن العدول عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r5.claim: Scholars disagree whether the Prophet himself is included in the address to believers; some include him, and leading Shafiʿis expressly require him to bless himself even in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r5.anchor: وفي دخوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في الخطاب بيا أيها الذين آمنوا هنا خلاف فقال بعضهم بالدخول

ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r6.claim: Reports show the Prophet blessing and saluting himself outside prayer, including when a hypocrite rejoiced that his camel was lost and when he discussed returning property taken from his son-in-law Abu al-As before the latter's conversion; narrator insertion is very unlikely.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p83#2/r6.anchor: كان يصلي على نفسه خارجها كما هو ظاهر أحاديث كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ضلت ناقته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r1.claim: Some exclude the Prophet from the address because its surrounding context runs from the command not to enter the Prophet's houses to this command; the author replies that the earlier command is explicitly restricted to believers, while this verse has no such restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r1.anchor: لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي ) إلى هنا ظاهرة في اختصاص هذا الحكم بالمؤمنين دونه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r2.claim: Usul scholars variously exclude the Prophet from such an address (a weak view), include him absolutely (called sound by a group), or include him except in commands to convey; the author includes him unless a contextual indicator excludes him, and finds such indicators here.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r2.anchor: وهو شاذ ودخوله مطلقا وهو الأصح على ما قال جمع والدخول

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r3.claim: Using believers rather than all people may signal that blessing the Prophet is a supreme and beneficial means unavailable to unbelievers; more likely, it both fits the context and urges believers to comply.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r3.anchor: وعبر بالذين آمنوا دون الناس الشامل للكفار قيل : إشارة إلى أن الصلاة عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r4.claim: The command to bless and salute the Prophet is a distinctive privilege of this community; no other community was commanded to bless and salute its prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r4.anchor: والأمر بالصلاة والتسليم من خواص هذه الأمة فلم تؤمر أمة غيرها بالصلاة والتسليم على نبيها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r5.speaker: أبو ذر الهروي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r5.claim: Abu Dharr al-Harawi reports that the command came in the second year after the Hijra; another view places it on the Night Journey, which the author regards as inconsistent with the verse's Medinan status.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r5.anchor: وكان ذلك على ما نقل عن أبي ذر الهروي في السنة الثانية من الهجرة وقيل : كان في ليلة الإسراء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r6.claim: Mujahid reports that when the verse was revealed Abu Bakr said every good thing sent to the Prophet was shared with them, after which the verse saying God and His angels bless the believers was revealed; the author says the differing styles have an evident wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r6.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن مجاهد أنها لما نزلت قال أبو بكر : ما أنزل الله عليك خيرا إلا أشركنا فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r7.claim: Blessing other prophets is permitted without dislike; a sound report, according to al-Majd al-Lughawi, tells people to include the Prophet when blessing the messengers, with another route judged good but mursal.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r7.anchor: والصلاة منا على الأنبياء ما عدا نبينا عليه وعليهم الصلاة والسلام جائزة بلا كراهة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r8.speaker: المجد اللغوي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r8.claim: The report also gives a wording: when people salute the Prophet, they should salute the messengers as well; the blessing wording has an additional good but mursal route.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84/r8.anchor: وفي لفظ إذا سلمتم علي فسلموا على المرسلين وللأول طريق أخرى إسنادها حسن جيد لكنه مرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r1.claim: No text is known specifically for blessing angels; the practice is inferred from Abu Hurayra's report if it is established that God called angels messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r1.anchor: لصلاة على الملائكة قيل لا يعرف فيها نص وإنما تؤخذ من حديث أبي هريرة المذكور آنفا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's instruction to bless God's prophets and messengers, whom God sent as He sent him; al-Alusi says its weak routes can be acted upon in this kind of matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : صلوا على أنبياء الله ورسله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r3.speaker: القاضي عياض
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r3.claim: On blessing people other than prophets and angels, Qadi Iyad says it is absolutely permitted, as do most scholars; he cites 33:43 and Prophetic prayers for families and individuals, including a woman and her husband.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r3.anchor: فقيل تجوز مطلقا قال القاضي عياض وعليه عامة أهل العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r4.claim: Evidence for general permission includes the Prophet's prayers for the family of Abu Awfa and the family of Saʿd ibn Ubada, and Ibn Hibban's sound report of a woman asking him to bless her and her husband.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r4.anchor: وبما صح من قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r5.speaker: مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r5.claim: A report in Muslim says angels tell the believer's soul, May God bless you and your body; this counters al-Khafaji's claim that angels bless the community only through following the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r5.anchor: وفي خبر مسلم أن الملائكة تقول لروح المؤمن : صلى الله عليك وعلى جسدك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r6.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r6.claim: Another view, chosen by al-Qurtubi and others, forbids blessing anyone independently but permits it in a textually established dependent form, such as for the Prophet's family, or by analogy for Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r6.anchor: وقيل لا تجوز استقلالا وتجوز تبعا فيما ورد فيه النص كالآل أو الحق به كالأصحاب وأختاره القرطبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r7.claim: A view attributed to Abu Hanifa and a group allows blessing others only dependently, never independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r7.anchor: وقيل تجوز تبعا مطلقا ولا تجوز استقلالا ونسب إلى أبي حنيفة وجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r8.speaker: البيري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r8.claim: The Hanafi text Tanwir al-Absar bars blessing anyone besides prophets and angels except dependently; al-Bayri says the ruling is sinful and disliked, and this is the sound position, while the exact degree of dislike is otherwise open to interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r8.anchor: وفي تنوير الأبصار ولا يصلي على غير الأنبياء والملائكة إلا بطريق التبع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r9.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r9.claim: A report from Ahmad regards independent blessing as disliked; the Shafiʿi position calls it خلاف الأولى.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r9.anchor: وفي رواية عن أحمد كراهة ذلك استقلالا ومذهب الشافعية أنه خلاف الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r10.speaker: القاضي عياض
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r10.claim: Al-Laqqani transmits Qadi Iyad's preference for restricting blessing and salutation to the Prophet and other prophets, with others instead mentioned through requests for forgiveness and approval as in 59:10; its use is said to have begun among early generations as a Rafidite innovation for some imams.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r10.anchor: أنه يجب تخصيص النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وسائر الأنبياء بالصلاة والتسليم كما يختص الله سبحانه عند ذكره بالتقديس

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r11.claim: Al-Alusi accepts that imitating innovators is disliked when the imitated act is blameworthy and the imitation is intended, but rejects a blanket application of that rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r11.anchor: ولا يخفى أن كراهة التشبه بأهل البدع مقررة عندنا أيضا لكن لا مطلقا بل في المذموم وفيما قصد به التشبه بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r12.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r12.claim: With a good or sound chain, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to his governor that storytellers had newly extended the Prophet's blessing to their allies and clients; he ordered prayer for prophets alone and general supplication for Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p84#2/r12.anchor: وجاء عن عمر بن عبدالعزيز بسند حسن أو صحيح أنه كتب لعامله إن ناسا من القصاص قد أحدثوا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas authentically says that no one should bless anyone except the Prophet; another version says to seek forgiveness for Muslim men and women instead. Both reports could indicate either dislike or prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r1.anchor: وصح عن ابن عباس أنه قال : لا تنبغي الصلاة من أحد على أحد إلا على النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r2.claim: Those who prohibit independent blessing argue that it became a distinctive honorific for prophets, just as عز وجل became a distinctive expression for God despite others being honored; they answer that God and His Messenger may grant such wording to whomever they choose, unlike others absent their permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r2.anchor: واستدل المانعون بأن لفظ الصلاة صار شعارا لعظم الأنبياء وتوقيرهم فلا تقال لغيرهم استقلالا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r3.speaker: أبو اليمن بن عساكر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r3.claim: Abu al-Yumn ibn Asakir says the Prophet may bless anyone because it is his prerogative and office, whereas the community may not bestow on another what belongs to him; the Shafiʿi Muʿtamad disputes that special privilege for lack of proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r3.anchor: ومن ثم قال أبو اليمن بن عساكر له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أن يصلي على غيره مطلقا لأنه حقه ومنصبه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r4.speaker: البيهقي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r4.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reconciles prohibition when blessing serves as an honorific greeting and permission when it is a prayer or request for blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r4.anchor: وحمل البيهقي بالمنع على ما إذا جعل ذلك تعظيما وتحية وبالجواز عليها إذا كان دعاء وتبركا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r5.speaker: بعض الحنابلة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r5.claim: Some Hanbalis allow independent blessing for the Prophet's family and general blessing for angels and the devout, but dislike or possibly forbid it for a named person or group, especially as an exclusive slogan for someone not equal or superior to the Prophet; occasional instances are allowed by Prophetic precedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r5.anchor: واختار بعض الحنابلة أن الصلاة على الآل مشروعة تبعا وجائزة استقلالا وعلى الملائكة وأهل الطاعة عموما جائزة أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r6.claim: The author says the evidence can be reconciled without that particular Hanbali distinction; many apply the same rules to salutation as to blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r6.anchor: وبهذا التفصيل تتفق الأدلة وأنت تعلم اتفاقها بغير ما ذكر والسلام عند كثير فيما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r7.speaker: الجويني
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r7.claim: Al-Juwayni, as quoted by al-Laqqani, treats salutation like blessing: it is not used of an absent person or independently for a non-prophet, so say Ali, may God be pleased with him, rather than peace be upon him; the author questions the claim of consensus, while direct greetings to those present are permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p85/r7.anchor: أنه في معنى الصلاة فلا يستعمل في الغائب ولا يفرد به غير الأنبياء عليهم السلام فلا يقال علي عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r1.speaker: الدر المنضود
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r1.claim: Al-Durr al-Mandud treats salutation like blessing, except for a present person or as a greeting to a living person who is absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r1.anchor: وفي الدر المنضود السلام كالصلاة فيما ذكر إلا إذا كان لحاضر أو تحية لحي غائب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r2.claim: Some distinguish salutation from blessing because it applies to every believer; the author calls this distinction circular and unsupported, and says the liturgical phrase peace upon us and God's righteous servants is a specific, dependent case.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r2.anchor: وفرق آخرون بأنه يشرع في حق كل مؤمن بخلاف الصلاة وهو فرق بالمدعي فلا يقبل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r3.speaker: التقي السبكي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r3.claim: A refined distinction, attributed to Taqi al-Subki, allows ordinary greeting to the living or dead at meetings or grave visits, with a response required of the present person or conveyed for the absent; salutation as a prayer that God grant peace is reserved for the Prophet except dependently.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r3.anchor: الذي يعم الحي والميت هو الذي يقصد به التحية كالسلام عند تلاق أو زيارة قبر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r4.speaker: الحليمي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r4.claim: The prayer-like salutation is what al-Halimi says is meant when he describes blessing as having the meaning of salutation; it requests that God confer peace and therefore carries a form of exaltation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r4.anchor: وهذا النوع من السلام هو الذي ادعى الحليمي كون الصلاة بمعناه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r5.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r5.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr forbids asking mercy for the Prophet; al-Alusi replies that sound hadiths attest it, including the tashahhud greeting with mercy and blessing, a Bedouin's prayer for himself and Muhammad that the Prophet approved, and other invocations.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r5.anchor: واختلف في جواز الدعاء له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالرحمة فذهب ابن عبدالبر إلى منع ذلك ورد بوروده في الأحاديث الصحيحة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r6.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r6.claim: A view taken by al-Suyuti and others, reported from the majority by Qadi Iyad and called correct by al-Qurtubi, permits asking mercy only when joined to blessing or salutation; al-Ghazali likewise forbids an unaccompanied request.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r6.anchor: وقد أخذ به جمع منهم الجلال السيوطي بل نقله القاضي عياض في الإكمال عن الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r7.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r7.claim: Al-Ghazali cites 24:63 and argues that, although blessing can mean mercy, prophets are distinguished by the honorific blessing, which for them is more specific than ordinary mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p86/r7.anchor: ويدل له قوله تعالى ( لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r1.speaker: ابن حجر الهيثمي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami says the Bedouin's prayer for mercy, approved by the Prophet, shows that mercy may be requested without accompanying blessing or salutation; this specific approval takes precedence over the verse's general implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r1.anchor: قال ابن حجر الهيثمي : وهو الذي يتجه وتقريره المذكور خاص فيقدم على العموم الذي اقتضته الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r2.speaker: ابن حجر الهيثمي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r2.claim: Ibn Hajar interprets those who say such a request is impermissible as denying neutral permissibility, allowing that it is disliked or خلاف الأولى; Zayn al-Din says they agree one should not initiate the formula may God have mercy on him, a recommendation al-Alusi endorses.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r2.anchor: وينبغي حمل قول من قال لا يجوز ذلك على أن مرادهم نفي الجواز المستوي الطرفين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r3.speaker: الطحطاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r3.claim: Al-Tahtawi advises against saying may God forgive or pardon the Prophet because it may imply a deficiency; al-Alusi leans the same way, while noting that seeking forgiveness need not imply sin and can request higher rank, as the Prophet sought forgiveness repeatedly.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r3.anchor: وينبغي أن لا يجوز غفر الله تعالى له أو سامحه لما فيه من إيهام النقص وهو الذي أميل إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r4.claim: The author's preferred caution against asking forgiveness or pardon does not mean such prayer entails a sin; the Quran's wording is God's prerogative, and mercy for angels should be treated like mercy for the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r4.anchor: وأرى حكم الترحم على الملائكة عليهم السلام كحكم الترحم عليه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r5.claim: For a person whose prophethood is disputed, such as Luqman, say may God be pleased with him, or include him in a prayer on the prophets, rather than independently assigning him the Prophet's formula.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p87/r5.anchor: ومن اختلف في نبوته كلقمان يقال فيه رضي الله تعالى عنه أو صلى الله تعالى على الأنبياء وعليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: Al-Tabrisi says adding to the Quran is universally rejected, while some Imamis and some Sunni traditionalists alleged omission; he says al-Murtada defended the correct denial of omission.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: أما الزيادة فيه أي القرآن فمجمع على بطلانها وأما النقصان فقد روى عن قوم من أصحابنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: Al-Murtada argues that reliable transmission of the Quran is as certain as knowledge of countries, major events, famous books, and recorded Arabic poetry, with still stronger motives to preserve it because it grounds prophecy and religious law.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: وذكر في مواضع أن العلم بصحة نقل القرآن كالعلم بالبلدان والحوادث الكبار والوقائع العظام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: He argues that Muslim scholars precisely tracked every difference in parsing, reading, letters, and verses, making alteration or loss implausible under their strong care and control.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: وعلماء المسلمين قد بلغوا في حفظه وحمايته الغاية حتى عرفوا كل شيء أختلف فيه من إعرابه وقراءته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: Knowledge of the Quran’s detailed parts is as certain as knowledge of the whole, like specialists’ knowledge of Sibawayh’s and al-Muzani’s books; an insertion would be detected, and care for Quran transmission was greater still.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: أن العلم بتفصيل القرآن وأبعاضه في صحة نقله كالعلم بجملته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Al-Murtada says the Quran was fully compiled and ordered in the Prophet’s lifetime: it was studied, memorized, recited to him, and repeatedly completed by Companions such as Ibn Masud and Ubayy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: وأن جماعة من الصحابة مثل عبدالله بن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وغيرهما ختموا القرآن على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عدة ختمات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r6.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r6.claim: Al-Tabrisi dismisses dissenting Imamis and traditionalists as not authoritative because they relied on weak reports they mistakenly considered sound, which cannot outweigh certain knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r6.anchor: لا يعتد بخلافهم فإن الخلاف في ذلك مضاف إلى قوم من أصحاب الحديث نقلوا أخبارا ضعيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says al-Tabrisi’s defense of Quranic integrity mixes falsehood into truth and falsely attributes an omission doctrine to Sunni traditionalists.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r7.anchor: إلا أن الرجل قد دس في الشهد سما وأدخل الباطل في حمى الحق الأحمى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r8.claim: Al-Alusi says Sunnis unanimously deny loss of any mass-transmitted Quranic text now between the covers; reports of omitted material refer instead to non-mutawatir readings, abrogated recitation, or material not present in the final review.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r8.anchor: لأنهم أجمعوا على قدم وقوع النقص فيما تواترا قرآنا كما هو موجود بين الدفتين اليوم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r9.speaker: حميدة بنت يونس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r9.claim: Humayda bint Yunus reports that Aisha’s codex included this verse followed by a phrase about those who pray in the first rows, before Uthman changed the codices; the excerpt gives no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p24/r9.anchor: كما روى عن حميدة بنت يونس أن في مصحف عائشة رضي الله عنها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's prayer as mercy for the Prophet and the angels' prayer as supplication for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد إن الله يرحم النبي، والملائكة يدعون له.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to explain “they pray” as seeking blessing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.claim: Another explanation says God's prayer is mercy and the angels' prayer is seeking forgiveness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الصلاة من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الاستغفار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says God's prayer is praise of the Prophet before the angels, while the angels pray for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: صلاة الله: ثناؤه عليه عند الملائكة، وصلاة الملائكة: الدعاء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r6.claim: Believers are to ask God for mercy upon the Prophet and greet him with the greeting of Islam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r6.anchor: أي: ادعوا له بالرحمة، {وسلموا تسليما} أي: حيوه بتحية الإسلام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r7.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r7.claim: Kaʿb reports that the Prophet taught them a formula asking blessings on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r7.anchor: لقيني كعب بن عجرة فقال: ألا أهدي لك هدية سمعتها من النبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r8.speaker: أبو حميد الساعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r8.claim: Abu Humayd reports that the Prophet taught a formula invoking blessing on Muhammad, his wives, and descendants as on Abraham's family.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p372#2/r8.anchor: أخبرني أبو حميد الساعي أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله كيف نصلي عليك؟ فقال رسول الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r1.claim: God and His angels show the Prophet's honor and magnify his rank.

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r2.claim: Believers should likewise show him care, saying, “O God, bless Muhammad.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r2.anchor: اعتنوا أنتم أيضا فإنكم أولى بذلك وقولوا اللهم صل على محمد

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r3.claim: Taslim may mean saying the greeting “Peace be upon you, Prophet,” or submitting to the Prophet's commands.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r3.anchor: وقولوا السلام عليك أيها النبي وقيل وانقادوا لأوامره

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r4.claim: The verse establishes that invoking blessing and peace upon the Prophet is obligatory at least in general.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r4.anchor: والآية تدل على وجوب الصلاة والسلام عليه في الجملة

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r5.claim: One view makes invoking blessing obligatory every time the Prophet is mentioned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r5.anchor: وقيل تجب الصلاة كلما جرى ذكره

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r6.claim: A Prophetic report condemns the person who hears the Prophet mentioned but fails to invoke blessing upon him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r6.anchor:
عليه الصلاة والسلام
" رغم أنف رجل ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي "

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r7.claim: Another Prophetic report prays that a person who hears the Prophet mentioned, fails to invoke blessing, and enters Hell be cast far away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r7.anchor:
عليه الصلاة والسلام
" رغم أنف رجل ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي "
وقوله
" من ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r8.claim: Blessing on another person is permitted when attached to the Prophet's blessing, but disliked by itself because custom has made it a distinctive formula for mentioning the Messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r8.anchor: على غيره تبعا. وتكره استقلالا لأنه في العرف صار شعارا لذكر الرسول

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r9.claim: For the same customary reason, it is disliked to call Muhammad “mighty and majestic,” although those descriptions are true of him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:56-57/r9.anchor: ولذلك كره أن يقال محمد عز وجل وإن كان عزيزا وجليلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r1.claim: God’s knowledge and action encompass all, and He possesses the greatest attributes of majesty, greatness, and might.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r1.anchor: أي وعملكم محيط بأن له مجامع الكبر والعظمة والعز

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r2.claim: The angels are beings of purity, nearness, and immunity from sin.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r2.anchor: أي وهم أهل النزهة والقرب والعصمة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r3.claim: Unlike 33:43, which gives God and the angels separate predicates, this verse joins them in one predicate for the Prophet, the highest addressee and head of believers, magnifying the statement.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r4.claim: A joint statement that two people support someone sounds grander than saying separately that one supports him and the other does so too.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r4.anchor: أضخم من قولك : فلان ينصره وفلان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r5.claim: The angels’ prayer displays the Prophet’s honor and connection to the supreme King through revelation of the wonders of the unseen and visible worlds.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r5.anchor: أي يظهرون شرفه وما له من الوصلة بالملك الأعظم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the angels’ prayer for the Prophet as their invoking blessings; al-Bukhārī transmits this gloss.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r6.anchor: وهو معنى قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كما وراه البخاري

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r7.claim: The verse’s close implies that believers are also to greet the Prophet, completing the connection conveyed by prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r7.anchor: علم بآخر الكلام أن المعنى : ويسلمون عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r8.claim: Believers should promptly and continually display his honor to substantiate their professed faith, as lovers imitate a revered leader.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r8.anchor: بعدم الغفلة عن المبادرة إلى إظهار شرفه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r9.claim: A great person’s action prompts each lover who recognizes his greatness to imitate him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r9.anchor: ولأن الكبير إذا فعل شيئا بادر كل محب له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r10.claim: Greeting the Prophet in the tashahhud is obligatory by consensus and signals submission to all his commands, which is necessary to faith; prayer is sought from God, while greeting comes from the worshipper.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r10.anchor: على الإذعان لجميع أوامره الذي لا يحصل الإيمان إلا به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r11.claim: The emphatic command calls for honoring the Prophet as fully as one can through following him, praising him, obeying him, and praying and greeting him as taught.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r11.anchor: أي فأظهورا شرفه بكل ما تصل قدرتكم إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r12.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وكعب بن عجزة
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r12.claim: Traditions from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, and others explain how prayer and greeting unite in displaying the Prophet’s honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r12.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري وكعب بن عجزة وغيرهما رضي الله عنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r13.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r13.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives prayer the senses of supplication, mercy, seeking forgiveness, and good praise from God; worshippers’ prayer includes bowing and prostration.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r14.speaker: البيضاوي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r14.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī traces greeting from a wish for life to a judgment or prayer for life, then to any invocation, with conventional use as a greeting.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r14.anchor: كما قال البيضاوي في تفسير سورة النساء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r15.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r15.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines greeting as peace, survival, or kingship, and “may God greet you” as “may He preserve you” or “make you king.”
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r15.anchor: وفي القاموس : التحية : السلام والبقاء والملك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r16.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r16.claim: Al-Qazzāz says salām is a name of God and here means safety: “peace be upon you” can mean no harm from me, or God’s safety, mercy, or protection from affliction.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r16.anchor: أبو عبد الله القزاز في جامعه : السلام اسم من أسماء الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r17.claim: The senses of prayer and greeting converge on displaying honor; al-Bayḍāwī similarly glosses prayer as displaying the Prophet’s honor and greeting as saying peace or submitting to his commands.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r17.anchor: فقد ظهر أن معنى الكل كما ترى ينظر إلى إظهار الشرف

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r18.speaker: البيضاوي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r18.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī interprets prayer as attending to the Prophet’s honor and greeting as either saying peace or submitting to his commands.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r18.anchor: ولذلك فسر البيضاوي يصلون بقوله : يعنتون بإظهار شرفه وتعظيم شأنه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r19.claim: Because prayer and greeting share the aim of displaying honor, Biqāʿī applies the word in both literal and figurative senses, following al-Shāfiʿī.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p132/r19.anchor: استعمالا للشيء في حقيقته ومجازه كما هو مذهب إمامنا الشافعي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r1.claim: Biqāʿī proposes iḥtibāk: emphasis after “pray” is omitted because the verbal noun after “greet” supplies it; the object of “greet” is omitted because “him” after “pray” supplies it, allowing “greet him” or “submit to him.”
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r1.anchor: فتقول : حذف التأكيد أولا لفعل الصلاة لما دل عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r2.claim: Biqāʿī says the root and forms of ṣalāt revolve around connection, which underlies the cited interpretations.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p133/r2.anchor: بجميع تراكيبها تدور على الوصلة وهي لازمة لكل ما ذكر

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God and the angels’ ṣalāt on the Prophet as blessing him.
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {يصلون} يتبركون

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God’s ṣalāt is praise of the Prophet before the angels, while the angels’ ṣalāt is supplication for him.
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه قال: صلاة الله عليه: ثناؤه عليه عند الملائكة وصلاة الملائكة عليه: الدعاء له

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Israelites asked Moses whether his Lord prays, God told him to answer yes, saying God and the angels pray for prophets and messengers; the verse was then revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن بني إسرائيل قالوا لموسى عليه السلام: هل يصلي ربك فناداه ربه يا موسى إن سألوك هل يصلي ربك فقل: نعم

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says people congratulated the Prophet; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said earlier blessings had been shared with the believers, unlike this verse, after which 9:112 was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {إن الله وملائكته} الآية قال: لما نزلت جعل الناس يهنؤنه بهذه الآية وقال أبي بن كعب: ما أنزل فيك خيرا

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says God’s ṣalāt on the Prophet means forgiveness, since God does not pray, while people’s ṣalāt means seeking forgiveness for him.
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في الآية قال: صلاة الله على النبي هي مغفرته إن الله لا يصلي ولكن يغفر

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r9.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to have read an expanded form: “Pray for him as God prayed for him, and give full peace.”
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ (صلوا عليه كما صلى عليه وسلموا تسليما)

DURR-FULL:v6p645/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r10.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r10.claim: When Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra asked how to pray for the Prophet, he was taught the formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family.
DURR-FULL:v6p645/r10.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزلت

DURR-FULL:v6p646/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have said this was how the verse was revealed; the Prophet taught a prayer and blessing formula for Muhammad and his family modeled on Abraham’s family.
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r1.anchor: عن يونس بن خباب قال: خطبنا بفارس فقال {إن الله وملائكته} الآية قال: انبأني من سمع ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يقول: هكذا انزل

DURR-FULL:v6p646/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r2.claim: Ibrahim reports that the Prophet answered the question about ṣalāt with a formula naming Muhammad, his household, and Abraham’s family, followed by a blessing formula.
