DURR-FULL:v6p646/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن الله وملائكته} قالوا: يا رسول الله هذا السلام قد عرفناه فكيف الصلاة عليك فقال: قولوا اللهم صل

DURR-FULL:v6p646/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي كثير بن أبي مسعود الأنصاري
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r3.claim: When asked how to pray for him despite his forgiveness, the Prophet prescribed asking God to bless Muhammad as He blessed Abraham and to bless Muhammad as He blessed Abraham’s family.
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي كثير بن أبي مسعود الانصاري رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزلت {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} قالوا: يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p646/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r4.speaker: رجل من أصحاب النبي
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r4.claim: A Companion’s formula asks God to bless Muhammad, his household, wives, and descendants as He blessed Abraham, and likewise to bless them.
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r4.anchor: عن رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: اللهم على محمد وعلى أهل بيته وعلى أزواجه وذريته كما صليت على إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v6p646/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r5.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r5.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports another Prophetic formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham’s family, then to bless them likewise.
DURR-FULL:v6p646/r5.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رجل يا رسول الله أما السلام عليك فقد علمناه فكيف الصلاة عليك قال قل اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد

DURR-FULL:v6p648/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r1.claim: The Prophet says whoever wants a full measure when praying for the Prophet’s household should ask God to bless Muhammad, his wives, descendants, and household as He blessed Abraham’s family.
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من سره أن يكتال بالمكيال الأوفى

DURR-FULL:v6p648/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r2.claim: The Prophet gives Ali a formula asking God to place prayers and mercy on Muhammad, his wives, descendants, and Mothers of the Believers as on Abraham.
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r2.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من سره أن يكتال بالمكيال الأوفى

DURR-FULL:v6p648/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r3.claim: The Prophet says a man receives daily reward equal to the deeds of earth’s inhabitants because he prays ten times each morning using a formula repeatedly invoking blessing on Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r3.anchor: عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه قال: كنت عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاءه رجل فسلم فرد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واطلق وجهه

DURR-FULL:v6p648/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r4.speaker: طلحة بن عبيد الله
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r4.claim: When Talha asked how to pray for him, the Prophet taught a formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family.
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r4.anchor: عن طلحة بن عبيد الله قال: قلت يا رسول الله كيف الصلاة عليك قال قل اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v6p648/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r5.speaker: طلحة بن عبيد الله
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r5.claim: Talha reports that a man who asked how to pray after hearing the verse was taught to invoke blessing on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham’s family.
DURR-FULL:v6p648/r5.anchor: عن طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه قال: أتى رجل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: سمعت الله يقول {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} فكيف الصلاة عليك

DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r1.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r1.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra asked how to pray after learning the greeting; the Prophet taught him to ask God to bless Muhammad and his family as Abraham’s family and to bless them likewise.
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r1.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزلت {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} قمت إليه فقلت: السلام عليك قد عرفناه

DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r2.claim: The Prophet tells Abu Saʿid al-Khudri to ask God to bless Muhammad as He blessed Abraham’s family and to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed them.
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: قلنا يا رسول الله هذا السلام عليك قد علمناه فكيف الصلاة عليك قال قولوا اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك

DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r3.claim: The Prophet’s answer asks for blessing on Muhammad and his family in the worlds as on Abraham and his family, adding that the greeting is already known.
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه انهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف نصلي عليك

DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r4.speaker: أبو مسعود الأنصاري
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r4.claim: When Bashir ibn Saʿd asked how to perform the commanded ṣalāt, the Prophet paused and then taught a formula blessing Muhammad and his family as Abraham was blessed; the greeting was already known.
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري رضي الله عنه أن بشير بن سعد قال: يا رسول الله أمرنا الله أن نصلي عليك فكيف نصلي عليك فسكت حتى تمنينا

DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r5.speaker: أبو حميد الساعدي
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r5.claim: The Prophet teaches a formula asking God to bless Muhammad, his wives, and descendants as He blessed Abraham, and to bless them likewise.
DURR-FULL:v6p648#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي حميد الساعدي رضي الله عنه أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله كيف نصلي عليك فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قولوا اللهم صل

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r1.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet taught the formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r1.anchor: عن علي قال: قلت يا رسول الله كيف نصلي عليك قال قولوا اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet taught asking God to place His prayers and blessings on Muhammad’s family as He placed them on Abraham’s family.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قلنا يا رسول الله قد علمنا كيف السلام عليك فكيف نصلي عليك قال قولوا اللهم اجعل صلواتك

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says that when someone recites this verse during prayer, he should pray for the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: إذا قال الرجل في الصلاة {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} فليصل عليه

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r4.speaker: أبو مسعود عقبة بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r4.claim: A man asked how to pray for the Prophet during prayer; the Prophet taught the formula blessing Muhammad and his family as Abraham’s family. Al-Hakim graded this report sound.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r4.anchor: عن أبي مسعود عقبة بن عمرو أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله أما السلام عليك فقد عرفناه فكيف نصلي عليك إذا نحن صلينا عليك في صلاتنا

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says a person should recite the tashahhud, pray for the Prophet, and then make supplication for himself.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: يتشهد الرجل ثم يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم يدعو لنفسه

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r6.claim: The Prophet says that a Muslim without charity may ask God to bless Muhammad and believing and Muslim men and women; this counts as charity for him.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أيما رجل مسلم لم يكن عنده صدقة

DURR-FULL:v6p649/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r7.claim: The Prophet says that whoever asks God to bless and show mercy to Muhammad and his family as to Abraham’s family will have the Prophet testify for him on Judgment Day and intercede for him.
DURR-FULL:v6p649/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قال: اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r1.speaker: غير مذكور
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r1.claim: The excerpt preserves a supplication asking that God’s prayers, mercy, and blessings on Muhammad and his family be as He made them on Abraham.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r1.anchor: صلواتك ورحمتك وبركاتك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما جعلتها على إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r2.claim: Mujahid reports the Prophet saying that believers are presented to him by their names and identities, so they should make their prayers for him excellent.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنكم تعرضون علي بأسمائكم ومسماكم فاحسنوا الصلاة علي

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r3.speaker: أبو طلحة
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r3.claim: Abu Talha reports that Gabriel told the Prophet each prayer for him earns ten good deeds, erases ten sins, raises ten degrees, is presented to him, and is returned with an equal response.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد عن أبي طلحة رضي الله عنه قال: دخلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فوجدته مسرورا فقلت: يا رسول الله ما أدري متى رأيتك أحسن بشرا

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r4.speaker: يعقوب بن زيد التيمي
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r4.claim: The Prophet says God sends ten prayers upon any servant who prays for him; when a man offers to devote all his supplication to the Prophet, he is told God will suffice his worldly and afterlife concerns.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r4.anchor: عن ابن عيينة قال: أخبرني يعقوب بن زيد التيمي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاني آت من ربي فقال: لا يصلي عليك عبد صلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r5.speaker: الحسن بن علي
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r5.claim: The Prophet says two angels seek forgiveness for a Muslim who prays for him and say “Amen” with God and the angels; if the Muslim does not pray for him, they ask that he not be forgiven.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r5.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنه قال: قالوا يا رسول الله أرأيت قول الله {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} قال إن هذا لمن المكتوم ولولا أنكم سألتموني عنه

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r6.claim: The Prophet says one prayer for him earns the worshipper ten prayers from God.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى علي واحدة صلى الله عليه عشرا

DURR-FULL:v6p652/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r7.claim: The Prophet says those who pray for him most will be closest to him on Judgment Day; al-Tirmidhi graded the report ḥasan.
DURR-FULL:v6p652/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أولى الناس بي يوم القيامة أكثرهم علي صلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p655/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r1.claim: Aisha advises people to adorn their gatherings with prayers for the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: زينوا مجالسكم بالصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v6p655/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r2.claim: Ibn Masud tells Zayd ibn Wahb not to omit praying for the Prophet a thousand times on Fridays, using the formula “O God, bless the unlettered Prophet.”
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن وهب قال: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه: يا زيد بن وهب لا تدع إذا كان يوم الجمعة أن تصلي على النبي ألف مرة

DURR-FULL:v6p655/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r3.claim: The Prophet commands believers to pray for God’s prophets and messengers, saying God sent them just as He sent him.
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال صلوا على أنبياء الله ورسله

DURR-FULL:v6p655/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says ṣalāt should be invoked only for the Prophet; Muslims should instead be asked forgiveness for.
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لا تصلح الصلاة على أحد إلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولكن يدعى للمسلمين والمسلمات بالاستغفار

DURR-FULL:v6p655/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r5.speaker: حميدة
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r5.claim: Hamida reports that Aisha’s codex placed the words “and those who arrange the first rows” after the verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p655/r5.anchor: عن حميدة قالت: أوصت لنا عائشة رضي الله عنها بمتاعها فكان في مصحفها {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} والذين يصفون الصفوف الأول

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r1.claim: In Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra’s report, the Prophet taught the formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family, and to bless them likewise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r1.anchor: يا رسول الله ، قد علمنا السلام عليك فكيف الصلاة عليك ؟ قال : ' قولوا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r2.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains God’s prayer as His being the All-Glorious and All-Holy, with the saying that His mercy preceded His wrath.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح : ان الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي قال : صلاته تبارك وتعالى سبوح قدوس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Israelites asked Moses whether his Lord prayed, God told him to answer that He and the angels pray for His prophets and messengers; this verse was then revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ان بني اسرائيل قالوا لموسى عليه السلام : هل يصلي ربك ؟

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r4.claim: In a second report from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā adds the supplication, “and us with them.”
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3151/r4.anchor: وكان عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى يقول : وعلينا معهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r1.claim: The address to believers is the verse’s purpose: after forbidding harm, it teaches that their duty goes further, requiring honor of the Messenger in words and conduct, by implication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r1.anchor: وجملة { يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه } هي المقصودة وما قبلها توطئة لها وتمهيد لأن الله لما حذر المؤمنين من كل ما يؤذي الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r2.claim: The present-tense verb suggests renewal and repetition, encouraging believers to repeat prayer upon the Prophet in imitation of God and the angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r2.anchor: وجيء في صلاة الله وملائكته بالمضارع الدال على التجديد والتكرير ليكون أمر المؤمنين بالصلاة عليه والتسليم عقب ذلك مشيرا إلى تكرير ذلك منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r3.claim: The command is to perform prayer, meaning supplication, but the manner of performing it is left unspecified here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r3.anchor: والأمر بالصلاة عليه معناه : إيجاد الصلاة ، وهي الدعاء ، فالأمر يؤول إلى إيجاد أقوال فيها دعاء وهو مجمل في الكيفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r4.claim: Ṣalāt means speaking well or saying words that bring good; supplication is its most familiar sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r4.anchor: والصلاة : ذكر بخير ، وأقوال تجلب الخير ، فلا جرم كان الدعاء هو أشهر مسميات الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r5.claim: God’s ṣalāt is His speech by which He decrees good for the Messenger, since supplication in its literal sense cannot apply to God; angels’ and people’s ṣalāt is supplication for forgiveness and mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r5.anchor: فصلاة الله : كلامه الذي يقدر به خيرا لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن حقيقة الدعاء في جانب الله معطل ، لأن الله هو الذي يدعوه الناس ، وصلاة الملائكة والناس : استغفار ودعاء بالرحمات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r6.speaker: أبو حميد الساعدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r6.claim: When the companions asked how to pray upon the Prophet after saying they knew the salutation, he instructed them to say the formula invoking blessing on Muhammad, his wives, and descendants as on Abraham; Malik transmits it in the Muwattaʾ from Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p97/r6.anchor: هذه رواية مالك في ( الموطأ ) عن أبي حميد الساعدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r1.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r1.claim: The majority regard prayer upon the Prophet in prayer, specifically the final tashahhud, as recommended; this is also the Shafiʿi position.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r1.anchor: وقال جمهور العلماء : هي في الصلاة مستحبة وهي في التشهد الأخير وهو الذي جرى عليه الشافعية أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r2.speaker: الخطابي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r2.claim: Al-Khattabi criticizes al-Shafiʿi’s position as lacking a predecessor model and opposing early practice; he says it was strongly censured.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r2.anchor: قال الخطابي : ولا أعلم للشافعي فيها قدوة وهو مخالف لعمل السلف قبله ، وقد شنع عليه في هذه المسألة جدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAshur clarifies that those who call it sunnah within prayer mean that it is recommended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r3.anchor: قلت : فمن قال إنها سنة في الصلاة فإنما أراد المستحب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r4.speaker: أهل الحديث
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r4.claim: Hadith scholars unanimously judged the report ‘There is no prayer for one who does not pray upon me’ weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r4.anchor: وأما حديث ( لا صلاة لمن لم يصل علي ) فقد ضعفه أهل الحديث كلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r5.claim: He recommends prayer upon the Prophet when he is mentioned, when opening books or letters, during supplication, at and after the call to prayer, on entering a mosque, and in the final tashahhud.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r5.anchor: ومن أسباب الصلاة عليه أن يصلي عليه من جرى ذكره عنده ، وكذلك في افتتاح الكتب والرسائل ، وعند الدعاء ، وعند سماع الأذان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r6.claim: The recurring present tense in the preface encourages frequent prayer upon the Prophet in imitation of God and the angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r6.anchor: وفي التوطئة للأمر بالصلاة على النبي بذكر الفعل المضارع في { يصلون } إشارة إلى الترغيب في الإكثار من الصلاة على النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAshur finds no evidence that the companions prayed upon the Prophet at every mention of his name, wrote the blessing whenever they wrote his name, or had an identifiable starting date for that writing practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r7.anchor: واعلم أنا لم نقف على أن أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا يصلون على النبي كلما جرى ذكر اسمه ولا أن يكتبوا الصلاة عليه إذا كتبوا اسمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r8.claim: He infers they prayed upon him when recalling aspects of his life, as people ask mercy for a deceased person when recalling his virtues.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r8.anchor: والذي يبدو أنهم كانوا يصلون على النبي إذا تذكروا بعض شؤونه كما كانوا يترحمون على الميت إذا ذكروا بعض محاسنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r9.speaker: عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r9.claim: Al-Halabi’s biography reports that after the Prophet’s death, Umar said, ‘We belong to God … God’s blessings be upon His Messenger,’ as Abu Bakr spoke to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r9.anchor: وفي ( السيرة الحلبية ) : ( لما توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واعترى عمر من الدهش ما هو معلوم وتكلم أبو بكر بما هو معلوم قال عمر : إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون صلوات الله على رسوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r10.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r10.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that Asmaʾ bint Abi Bakr prayed for God’s blessing and peace upon Muhammad whenever she passed al-Hajun, recalling their time there with him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p99/r10.anchor: وروى البخاري في باب : متى يحل المعتمر : عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر أنها كانت تقول كلما مرت بالحجون ( صلى الله على رسوله محمد وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r1.claim: The command to offer salutation matches prayer upon the Prophet in ruling, occasion, and form; the known formula is ‘Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and God’s mercy and blessings.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وسلموا تسليما } القول فيه كالقول في { صلوا عليه } حكما ومكانا وصفة فإن صفته حددت بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( والسلام كما قد علمتم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r2.claim: Ibn Umar used ‘Peace be upon the Prophet and God’s mercy and blessings’ after the Prophet’s death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r2.anchor: وكان ابن عمر يقول فيه بعد وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( السلام على النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r3.claim: The majority retained the wording used while the Prophet was alive, relying on the report that he lives and receives his community’s salutations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r3.anchor: والجمهور أبقوا لفظه على اللفظ الذي كان في حياة النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام رعيا لما ورد عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه حي يبلغه تسليم أمته عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r4.claim: The living-address formula places the salutation before its recipient, unlike the formula for the dead, which puts the prepositional phrase before ‘peace.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r4.anchor: ومن أجل هذا المعنى أبقيت له صيغة التسليم على الأحياء وهي الصيغة التي يتقدم فيها لفظ التسليم على المتعلق به لأن التسليم على الأموات يكون بتقديم المجرور على لفظ السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r5.claim: When a man greeted him ‘Upon you be peace, Messenger of God,’ the Prophet said that ‘upon you be peace’ is the greeting of the dead and instructed him to say ‘Peace be upon you.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r5.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم للذي سلم عليه فقال : عليك السلام يا رسول الله فقال له : ( إن عليك السلام تحية الموتى ، فقل : السلام عليك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r6.claim: Salām is a greeting meaning safety and peace; it began as mutual assurance against attack or vengeance, then became a mark of honor and kindness, as al-Nabigha’s verse illustrates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r6.anchor: والتسليم مشهور في أنه التحية بالسلام ، والسلام فيه بمعنى الأمان والسلامة ، وجعل تحية في الأولين عند اللقاء مبادأة بالتأمين من الاعتداء والثأر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r7.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r7.claim: Al-Nabigha’s verse uses ‘greeting and peace’ as the courtesy people exchange.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r7.anchor: قال النابغة : أتاركة تدللها قطام وضنا بالتحية والسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r8.claim: Because salutation was already familiar, the companions did not ask its form; the command is to address peace to the Prophet, not to ask God to grant him peace as with prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p101/r8.anchor: ولذلك كان قوله تعالى : { وسلموا } غير مجمل ولا محتاج إلى بيان فلم يسأل عنه الصحابة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقالوا : هذا السلام قد عرفناه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r1.claim: Sunni convention permits including the Prophet’s family, companions, and righteous believers after him in the blessing, but not blessing them independently; this distinguishes religious ranks rather than prohibiting it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r1.anchor: وأنه يجوز إتباع آلهم وأصحابهم وصالحي المؤمنين إياهم في ذلك دون استقلال . هذا الذي استقر عليه اصطلاح أهل السنة ولم يقصدوا بذلك تحريما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r2.claim: The convention parallels limiting ‘may God be pleased with him’ to companions and imams and exaltation formulas such as ‘glory be to Him’ to the Creator alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r2.anchor: كما قصروا الرضى على الأصحاب وأيمة الدين ، وقصروا كلمات الإجلال نحو : تبارك وتعالى ، وجل جلاله ، على الخالق دون الأنبياء والرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAshur opposes the Shiʿi practice of invoking salutation on Ali, Fatima, and their family, saying it departs from early practice and aims to diminish the caliphs and companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r3.anchor: وأما الشيعة فإنهم يذكرون التسليم على علي وفاطمة وآلهما ، وهو مخالف لعمل السلف فلا ينبغي اتباعهم فيه لأنهم قصدوا به الغض من الخلفاء والصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r4.claim: ‘Tasliman’ is an emphatic cognate accusative for ‘sallimu’; prayer is not similarly emphasized because ṣalāt chiefly functions as a noun and its verbal noun, taṣliya, was avoided because it became associated with burning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r4.anchor: وانتصب { تسليما } على أنه مصدر مؤكد ل { سلموا } وإنما لم يؤكد الأمر بالصلاة عليه بمصدر فيقال : صلوا عليه صلاة ، لأن الصلاة غلب إطلاقها على معنى الاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r5.claim: Although it lacks formal cognate-accusative emphasis, the preceding statement that God and angels pray upon the Prophet urges believers to imitate them and emphatically supports the command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r5.anchor: على أن الأمر بالصلاة عليه قد حصل تأكيده بالمعنى لا بالتأكيد الاصطلاحي فإن التمهيد له بقوله : { إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي } مشير إلى التحريض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r6.claim: After warning against subtle and overt harm to the Prophet and teaching respect, the passage announces the blessing, then warns of people who appear Muslim yet pursue harm; its severe curse exposes them as hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p103/r6.anchor: لما أرشد الله المؤمنين إلى تناهي مراتب حرمة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتكريمه وحذرهم مما قد يخفى على بعضهم من خفي الأذى في جانبه بقوله : { إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r1.claim: The verse honors the Messenger, states his rank before God, and clears him of suspicion concerning his wives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية شرف الله بها رسوله عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r2.claim: One group takes the pronoun in yuṣallūna as referring jointly to God and the angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r2.anchor: قالت فرقة الضمير فيه لله وللملائكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r3.claim: Another group supplies an ellipsis: God blesses the Prophet and angels bless him, so the pronoun does not combine them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة: في الكلام حذف تقديره إن الله يصلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r4.claim: A third group says joining God and angels in one pronoun is permissible; the preacher was criticized for pausing after “whoever disobeys them.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل جمع الله تعالى الملائكة مع نفسه في ضمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r5.claim: Abu Dawud’s version has the Prophet say “whoever disobeys them”; Muslim’s report tells the preacher to name God and His Messenger separately.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p397#2/r5.anchor: ومما يؤيد هذا أن في كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مصنف أبي داود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Prophet may have corrected the preacher’s pause then improved the whole wording; separating pronouns is preferable though joining is allowed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r1.anchor: «بئس الخطيب أنت» لموضع) خطأه في الوقف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r2.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r2.claim: The majority read the final tāʾ of malāʾikatahu in the accusative, coordinating it with the explicit noun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reads malāʾikatuhu in the nominative, coordinating it with the syntactic position before inna; Ibn Atiyya questions this.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r4.claim: God’s ṣalāt is mercy and blessing; angels’ is supplication; believers’ is supplication and reverence.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r5.claim: Sending blessings at all times is an emphatic sunnah duty that should not be neglected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r5.anchor: والصلاة على رسول الله في كل حين من الواجبات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r6.claim: The Prophet urged frequent blessings on him on Friday, a witnessed day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r6.anchor: وقال عليه السلام: «أكثروا من الصلاة علي يوم الجمعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that companions asked how to send blessings; the Prophet taught a prayer invoking blessings on Muhammad’s family as on Abraham’s.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r7.anchor: من طريق ابن عباس أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r8.claim: The prayer asks for mercy and blessing on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham’s; reports vary in wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r8.anchor: وارحم محمدا وآل محمد كما رحمت وباركت على إبراهيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r9.claim: Al-Hasan reads faṣallū with an added fāʾ, strengthening the conditional sense: God blesses, so you bless.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «يا أيها الذين آمنوا فصلوا عليه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r10.speaker: عبد الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r10.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah adds “as God has blessed him” before the greeting command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p398/r10.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله «صلوا عليه كما صلى الله عليه وسلموا تسليما»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers to earlier explanations in this sura for the meanings of God's and the angels' ṣalāt upon the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r1.anchor: في صلاة الله وصلاة الملائكة أقوال قد تقدمت في هذه السورة الأحزاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r2.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r2.claim: Ka'b ibn Ujra reports that the Companions asked how to pray for the Prophet after learning the salutation; he taught the formula asking blessing and honor for Muhammad and his family as for Abraham's family. Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r2.anchor: قال كعب بن عجرة قلنا يا رسول الله قد عرفنا التسليم عليك فكيف الصلاة عليك فقال قولوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r3.claim: The Companions' known salutation is the tashahhud wording, peace be upon you, O Prophet, with God's mercy and blessings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى قوله قد علمنا التسليم عليك ما يقال في التشهد السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r4.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib interprets the command to offer salutation as submitting to what the Prophet commands.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p418#2/r4.anchor: وذهب ابن السائب إلى أن معنى التسليم سلموا لما يأمركم به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God's salat is praise of the Prophet among the angels, while the angels' salat is supplication.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r1.anchor: قال أبو العالية: صلاة الله: ثناؤه عليه عند الملائكة، وصلاة الملائكة: الدعاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses yusalluna as they bless him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r3.speaker: سفيان الثوري وغير واحد من أهل العلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r3.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri and other scholars say the Lord's salat means mercy and the angels' salat means seeking forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r3.anchor: قالوا: صلاة الرب: الرحمة، وصلاة الملائكة: الاستغفار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r4.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r4.claim: A report from Ata ibn Abi Rabah gives God's words as: Holy, Most Holy; My mercy has preceded My anger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r4.anchor: عن عطاء (2) بن أبي رباح {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي} قال: صلاته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r5.claim: God announces the Prophet's rank in the highest assembly, praising him before the angels; He then commands earthly people to pray and greet him, uniting praise from both realms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r5.anchor: بأنه يثني عليه عند الملائكة المقربين، وأن الملائكة تصلي عليه. ثم أمر تعالى أهل العالم السفلي بالصلاة والتسليم عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Israelites asked Moses whether God prays, God told him to answer that He and His angels pray upon prophets and messengers; Ibn Kathir says this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن بني إسرائيل قالوا لموسى عليه السلام: هل يصلي ربك؟ فناداه ربه: يا موسى، سألوك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir links the verse to 33:41–43, which says God and His angels pray upon believers and that He brings them from darkness to light.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r7.anchor: يصلي على عباده المؤمنين في قوله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r8.claim: He also connects it to 2:155–157, where those who endure calamity receive blessings and mercy from their Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r8.anchor: وقال تعالى: {وبشر الصابرين (5) . الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r9.claim: A hadith says God and His angels pray upon the right sides of the prayer rows.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث: "إن الله وملائكته يصلون على ميامن الصفوف"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r10.claim: The Prophet's supplication for the family of Abu Awfa is cited as an example of salat being requested for others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر: "اللهم، صل على آل أبي أوفى"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r11.claim: When Jabir's wife asked the Prophet to pray for her and her husband, he said, May God pray upon you and your husband.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p457/r11.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لامرأة جابر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says numerous, mass-transmitted reports teach both the command to pray upon the Prophet and its wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r1.anchor: وقد جاءت الأحاديث المتواترة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأمر بالصلاة عليه، وكيفية الصلاة عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r2.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r2.claim: Asked how to pray after learning the greeting, the Prophet taught the formula asking blessings on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham's family, and blessings for them as for Abraham's family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r2.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة قال: قيل: يا رسول الله، أما السلام عليك فقد عرفناه، فكيف الصلاة؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r3.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p458/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits the same teaching through Ka'b; Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla would add, And us with them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits an added phrase to the Ka'b report: include us among them in the prayer for blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r1.anchor: ورواه الترمذي بهذه الزيادة (1) . ومعنى قولهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r2.claim: The greeting they already knew is the salutation in the tashahhud, which the Prophet taught them as he taught a Quranic surah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r2.anchor: هو الذي في التشهد الذي كان يعلمهم إياه، كما كان يعلمهم السورة من القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r3.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet's formula: pray on Muhammad, God's servant and messenger, as on Abraham's family, and bless Muhammad and his family as Abraham's family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، رضي الله عنه، قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله، هذا السلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r4.speaker: أبو حميد الساعدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r4.claim: Abu Humayd reports a formula asking that blessings and benedictions be upon Muhammad, his wives, and descendants as upon Abraham's family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن سليم أنه قال: أخبرني أبو حميد الساعدي أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله، كيف نصلي عليك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r5.speaker: أبو مسعود الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r5.claim: At Sa'd ibn Ubada's gathering, Bashir ibn Sa'd asked how to pray on the Prophet; after a pause, the Prophet taught the formula and said to give the greeting already taught.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459/r5.anchor: أخبره عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري -قال: أتانا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Abu Masud report transmitted through Malik as hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r1.anchor: من حديث مالك، به (11) . وقال الترمذي: حسن صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r2.speaker: أبو مسعود البدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r2.claim: A further Abu Masud report asks how to pray on the Prophet in prayer and gives the formula asking blessings upon Muhammad and his family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي مسعود البدري أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله، أما السلام فقد عرفناه، فكيف نصلي عليك إذا نحن صلينا في صلاتنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i rules that prayer upon the Prophet is obligatory in the final tashahhud and that omitting it invalidates the prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r3.anchor: ذهب الشافعي، رحمه الله، إلى أنه يجب على المصلي أن يصلي على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في التشهد الأخير، فإن تركه لم تصح صلاته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r4.speaker: بعض المتأخرين من المالكية وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r4.claim: Some later Malikis and others say al-Shafi'i was alone and cite al-Tabari, al-Tahawi, and al-Khattabi for a consensus against his requirement; Ibn Kathir calls this overreaching.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r4.anchor: ويزعم أنه قد تفرد بذلك، وحكى الإجماع على خلافه أبو جعفر الطبري والطحاوي والخطابي وغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says the verse and hadith support al-Shafi'i; Companions, Successors, and later authorities also held the prayer obligatory, so no consensus opposes him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r5.anchor: فإنه قد روينا وجوب ذلك والأمر بالصلاة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة كما هو ظاهر الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r6.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق بن راهويه وابن المواز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir names Ahmad in his later view, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and the Maliki Ibn al-Mawwaz among those who required prayer upon the Prophet in prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r6.anchor: أحمد أخيرا فيما حكاه عنه أبو زرعة الدمشقي، به. وبه قال إسحاق بن راهويه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r7.speaker: بعض أئمة الحنابلة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r7.claim: Some Hanbali authorities required the exact wording the Prophet taught when people asked how to pray on him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r7.anchor: حتى إن بعض أئمة الحنابلة أوجب أن يقال في الصلاة عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم كما علمهم أن يقولوا لما سألوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r8.speaker: البندنيجي وسليم الرازي ونصر بن إبراهيم المقدسي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r8.claim: Some Shafi'i authorities held that prayer on the Prophet's family is obligatory too; Ibn Kathir calls this one valid school position, though the majority disagree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p459#2/r8.anchor: حتى إن بعض أصحابنا أوجب الصلاة على الآل ممن (8) حكاه البندنيجي، وسليم الرازي، وصاحبه نصر بن إبراهيم المقدسي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reiterates that al-Shafi'i had predecessors and successors, so there is no early or later consensus against the obligation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r1.anchor: والغرض أن الشافعي، رحمه الله، لقوله (9) بوجوب الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r2.speaker: فضالة بن عبيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r2.claim: Fadala reports that the Prophet corrected a supplicant who had not praised God or prayed on the Prophet, teaching him first to praise God, then pray on the Prophet, then make any supplication; al-Tirmidhi graded it sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r2.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد، رضي الله عنه، قال: سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يدعو في صلاته، لم يمجد الله ولم يصل على النبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r3.claim: A report says there is no prayer without prayer upon the Prophet, but its transmitter Abd al-Muhaymin is abandoned; the al-Tabarani route through his brother is questionable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r3.anchor: من رواية عبد المهيمن بن عباس بن سهل بن سعد الساعدي، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r4.speaker: بريدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r4.claim: Burayda reports a formula asking God's prayers, mercy, and blessings for Muhammad and his family as for Abraham's family; Ibn Kathir notes the transmitter Abu Dawud al-A'ma is abandoned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r4.anchor: عن بريدة قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله، قد علمنا كيف نسلم عليك، فكيف نصلي عليك؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r5.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r5.claim: A report attributed to Ali gives a lengthy invocation asking God for abundant prayers and blessings upon Muhammad, describing him as the seal of what came before and opener of what was closed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p460/r5.anchor: أن عليا، رضي الله عنه، كان يعلم الناس هذا الدعاء: اللهم داحي المدحوات، وبارئ المسموكات، وجبار القلوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r1.speaker: الحافظ أبو الحجاج المزي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r1.claim: Al-Mizzi says Salama al-Kindi is unknown and did not meet Ali, so the chain for the lengthy invocation attributed to Ali is problematic; Ibn Kathir notes al-Tabarani's route too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا الحافظ أبو الحجاج المزي: سلامة (4) الكندي هذا ليس بمعروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says to make the prayer upon the Prophet excellent, since one cannot know whether it will be presented to him, then teaches an extended formula of salat and blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: إذا صليتم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأحسنوا الصلاة عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو أو عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r3.claim: Ismail al-Qadi transmits a similar stopped report from Abd Allah ibn Amr or Umar, with the narrator uncertain between the two.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو -أو: عمر -على الشك من الراوي قريبا من هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed as stated, then gives a formula asking for prayer, mercy, and blessings on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham's family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p462/r4.anchor: أنبأني من سمع ابن عباس يقول: هكذا أنزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir treats the report and the Bedouin's prayer as support for permissibility of invoking mercy on the Prophet, which he says is the majority view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r1.anchor: فيستدل بهذا الحديث من ذهب إلى جواز الترحم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما هو قول الجمهور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r2.speaker: القاضي عياض
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r2.claim: Qadi Iyad reports that most Malikis prohibit invoking mercy on the Prophet, while Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Zayd permits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r2.anchor: وحكى القاضي عياض عن جمهور المالكية منعه، قال: وأجازه أبو محمد بن أبي زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r3.claim: A Bedouin asked Allah to show mercy to him and Muhammad alone; the Prophet replied that he had restricted a vast mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r4.speaker: عامر بن ربيعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r4.claim: عامر بن ربيعة reports the Prophet saying that angels continue praying for whoever prays for him, whether the person does so little or much; Ibn Majah also transmits it through Shuʿba.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r4.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة يحدث عن أبيه قال: سمعت النبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r5.claim: Two Ahmad routes from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf recount the Prophet's long prostration and Gabriel's message that God blesses whoever blesses the Prophet and greets whoever greets him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p463/r5.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتبعته حتى دخل نخلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r1.claim: Umar found the Prophet prostrating; Gabriel conveyed that one prayer from a member of the community earns ten divine prayers and ten degrees. Al-Diya al-Maqdisi selected this report in his Mustakhraj on the Sahihayn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r1.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لحاجة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet saying that those who pray for him most will be nearest to him on the Day of Resurrection; al-Tirmidhi alone transmits it and calls it hasan gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r3.speaker: يعقوب بن زيد بن طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r3.claim: Yaqub ibn Zayd ibn Talha relays a report that praying for the Prophet earns ten divine prayers and that dedicating one's whole prayer to him lets God suffice one's worldly and next-world concerns; Sufyan did not know its transmitter link.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p464/r3.anchor: عن يعقوب بن زيد بن طلحة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asks how much of his prayer to devote to the Prophet; the versions increase the suggested share from a third to all, with the all-prayer version promising forgiveness or relief from anxieties. Al-Tirmidhi grades his version hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r1.anchor: عن الطفيل بن أبي بن كعب، عن أبيه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخرج في جوف الليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r2.claim: Ahmad transmits Ubayy's shorter version: a man asks whether making all his prayer for the Prophet will suffice, and is told that God will suffice his worldly and next-world concerns.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r2.anchor: عن الطفيل بن أبي، عن أبيه قال: قال رجل: يا رسول الله، أرأيت إن جعلت صلاتي كلها عليك؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r3.speaker: أبو طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r3.claim: Abu Talha reports that an angel told the Prophet that God blesses ten times whoever from his community prays for him, and returns tenfold greeting to whoever greets him; the Prophet assented.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p465/r3.anchor: عن أبيه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء ذات يوم، والسرور يرى في وجهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r1.speaker: أبو طلحة الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r1.claim: In Ahmad's other report, Gabriel says one prayer for the Prophet earns ten good deeds, erases ten sins, raises ten degrees, and is returned in kind; Ibn Kathir calls its chain good, though the canonical collectors omit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r1.anchor: عن أبي طلحة الأنصاري قال: أصبح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما طيب النفس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever prays for the Prophet once receives ten divine prayers; al-Tirmidhi grades this report hasan sahih, and Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasaʾi also transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r2.anchor: عن أبيه؛ عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r3.claim: Ahmad's Abu Hurayra report calls prayer for the Prophet a purification for the worshipper and says to ask God for al-wasila, the highest Garden's rank, which the Prophet hopes to receive.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r3.anchor: عن كعب، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r4.claim: Al-Bazzar's parallel from Mujahid and Abu Hurayra likewise urges prayer and asking for al-wasila, described as the highest Garden's single rank that the Prophet hopes will be his.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p466/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some transmitters criticize the chain of al-Bazzar's preceding report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r1.anchor: في إسناده بعض من تكلم فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r2.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr reports that one prayer for the Prophet brings seventy prayers from God and the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r2.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عمرو يقول: من صلى على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r3.claim: In a separate farewell-like report, the Prophet says he is the unlettered final prophet, has been given comprehensive speech and knowledge of Hell's keepers and Throne-bearers, and tells the community to obey him then follow God's Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r3.anchor: وسمعت عبد الله بن عمرو يقول: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما كالمودع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r4.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that whoever hears his name mentioned should pray for him, and that one prayer earns ten divine prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r5.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r5.claim: A second report from Anas says one prayer for the Prophet brings ten divine prayers and removes ten sins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467/r5.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r1.speaker: الحسين بن علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the report that a miser is one who hears the Prophet mentioned but does not pray for him as hasan gharib sahih; transmitters differ whether its Companion source is al-Husayn or Ali.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r1.anchor: ورواه الترمذي من حديث سليمان بن بلال، ثم قال: هذا حديث حسن غريب صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some transmitters attribute the miser report to al-Husayn ibn Ali, while others make it a report from Ali himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r2.anchor: ومن الرواة من جعله من مسند

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r3.claim: Abu Dharr reports from the Prophet that the most miserly person is one who hears the Prophet mentioned but does not pray for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r3.anchor: عن عوف بن مالك، عن أبي ذر، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r4.claim: Hasan al-Basri gives a mursal version: sufficient miserliness is for a person to be mentioned and not pray for the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r4.anchor: حدثنا جرير بن حازم، سمعت الحسن يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports three disgraced people: one who hears the Prophet mentioned without praying for him, one who lets Ramadan pass unforgiven, and one whose aged parents do not admit him to Paradise. Al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan gharib; al-Bukhari and other routes also transmit it, with several other Companions cited.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir takes this and the preceding report as evidence that praying for the Prophet is obligatory every time he is mentioned; he attributes this view to a group including al-Tahawi and al-Hulaymi and cites a corroborating Ibn Majah report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p467#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الحديث والذي قبله دليل على وجوب الصلاة عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم كلما ذكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for the report that forgetting prayer for the Prophet makes one miss the path to Paradise. Ibn Majah's Jabara route is weak; al-Baqir's mursal version is said to gain support from the earlier report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r1.anchor: من نسي الصلاة علي خطئ طريق الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r2.claim: Another view requires one prayer for the Prophet per sitting and recommends it for the rest of that sitting; Ibn Kathir says a report from Abu Hurayra supports this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r2.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أنه تجب الصلاة في المجلس مرة واحدة، ثم لا تجب في بقية ذلك المجلس، بل تستحب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a gathering without remembrance of God or prayer for the Prophet incurs loss and may be punished or forgiven; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r4.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that people who disperse without praying for the Prophet will regret it, even if they enter Paradise when they see the reward they missed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r4.anchor: عن ذكوان، عن أبي سعيد قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r5.speaker: القاضي عياض
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r5.claim: Qadi Iyad upholds the view that the verse requires prayer for the Prophet once in a lifetime and recommends more. He reads al-Tabarani's reported consensus for recommendation as applying beyond the obligatory once, comparable to testimony to prophethood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p468/r5.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه إنما تجب الصلاة عليه، عليه السلام، في العمر مرة واحدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the lifetime-once position strange because prayer for the Prophet is commanded at many times, some obligatory and others recommended.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r1.anchor: قلت: وهذا قول غريب، فإنه قد ورد الأمر بالصلاة عليه في أوقات كثيرة، فمنها واجب، ومنها مستحب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r2.claim: The Prophet instructs listeners to answer the caller to prayer, then pray for him and ask God for al-wasila; whoever asks it for him earns his intercession, and the Prophet hopes to receive that Garden rank.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r2.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص يقول: أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r3.claim: A second report from Abd Allah ibn Amr says that whoever asks God to grant the Prophet al-wasila is entitled to the Prophet's intercession on Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r3.anchor: عن صفوان بن سليم، عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r4.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra urges prayer for the Prophet as purification and asking God for al-wasila, the Garden's highest rank reserved for one man whom the Prophet hopes to be.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r4.anchor: عن كعب -هو كعب الأحبار -عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r5.speaker: رويفع بن ثابت الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r5.claim: Ruwayfiʿ ibn Thabit reports that whoever prays for Muhammad and asks God to place him at the honored station near Him on Judgment Day earns the Prophet's intercession.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p469/r5.anchor: عن رويفع بن ثابت الأنصاري؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ruwayfiʿ's report has an acceptable chain, though the canonical collectors do not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد لا بأس به، ولم يخرجوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas offers a supplication asking God to accept Muhammad's great intercession, raise his rank, grant his requests in both lives, and give him as He gave Abraham and Moses; Ibn Kathir calls its chain good, strong, and sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r2.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: اللهم تقبل شفاعة محمد الكبرى، وارفع درجته العليا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r3.speaker: فاطمة بنت رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r3.claim: Fatima reports that the Prophet prayed for himself when entering and leaving the mosque, then asked forgiveness and for the gates of mercy on entry and bounty on exit to be opened.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r3.anchor: عن جدته [فاطمة] (12) بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r4.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib said that when passing mosques people should pray for the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r4.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين قال: قال علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that scholars including al-Shafiʿi require prayer for the Prophet in the final tashahhud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r5.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى ذلك من العلماء مع (3) الشافعي، رحمه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r6.claim: The first tashahhud is unanimously not obligatory; whether prayer for the Prophet is recommended there is disputed in two Shafiʿi positions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r6.anchor: وأما التشهد الأول فلا تجب فيه قولا واحدا، وهل تستحب؟ على قولين للشافعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r7.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r7.claim: The funeral-prayer practice is to recite al-Fatiha after the first takbir, pray for the Prophet after the second, supplicate for the deceased after the third, and make a closing supplication after the fourth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p470/r7.anchor: أن السنة في الصلاة على الجنازة أن يكبر الإمام، ثم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب بعد التكبيرة الأولى سرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r1.claim: Al-Nasaʾi gives Abu Umama's wording that this funeral-prayer order is Sunna; Ibn Kathir says a Companion's statement here counts as marfuʿ according to the sound view. A route via Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and similar reports from Abu Hurayra, Ibn Umar, and al-Shaʿbi are also noted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r1.anchor: ورواه النسائي، عن أبي أمامة نفسه أنه قال: من السنة، فذكره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r2.claim: Ibn Masud describes the Eid prayer's sequence: each cycle opens with takbir, praise, prayer for the Prophet, and supplication; after the first cycle's recitation and bowing, the second repeats the praise, prayer, supplication, and takbirs. Hudhayfa and Abu Musa affirm him; the chain is sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r2.anchor: أن ابن مسعود وأبا موسى وحذيفة خرج عليهم الوليد بن عقبة يوما قبل العيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r3.claim: Umar is quoted by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib as saying supplication remains suspended between heaven and earth until one prays for the Prophet; another route also preserves it as Umar's own statement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r3.anchor: عن أبي قرة الأسدي، عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن عمر بن الخطاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r4.claim: Other transmissions raise the suspended-supplication report to the Prophet and add: pray for him at the beginning, middle, and end of supplication, and do not treat him like a rider's waterskin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p471/r4.anchor: ورواه معاذ بن الحارث، عن أبي قرة، عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن عمر مرفوعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r1.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet’s analogy of a rider’s cup and instruction to place him at the beginning, middle, and end of supplication.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r1.anchor: قال جابر: قال لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تجعلوني كقدح الراكب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report strange and Musa ibn Ubayda weak in hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r2.anchor: فهذا حديث غريب، وموسى بن عبيدة ضعيف الحديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r3.claim: He cites the Witr qunut supplication as an especially emphasized setting connected with sending blessings on the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r3.anchor: ذلك: دعاء القنوت: لما رواه الإمام أحمد وأهل السنن، وابن خزيمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r4.speaker: الحسن بن علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r4.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reports that the Prophet taught him the Witr supplication beginning with a request for guidance and ending in praise of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي، رضي الله عنهما، قال: علمني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمات أقولهن في الوتر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r5.speaker: النسائي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r5.claim: Al-Nasa'i's version adds a closing invocation asking God to bless Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r5.anchor: وزاد النسائي في سننه بعد هذا: وصلى الله على النبي محمد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r6.claim: He recommends frequent blessings upon the Prophet on Friday and its eve.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك: أنه يستحب الإكثار من الصلاة عليه [في] (4) يوم الجمعة وليلة الجمعة:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r7.speaker: أوس بن أوس الثقفي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r7.claim: Aws reports that Friday is the best day, prayers are presented to the Prophet then, and the earth is forbidden to consume prophets’ bodies when asked how prayers reach him after decay.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r7.anchor: عن أوس بن أوس الثقفي، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أفضل أيامكم يوم الجمعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban, al-Daraqutni, and al-Nawawi authenticated the Friday report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p472/r8.anchor: وقد صحح هذا الحديث ابن خزيمة وابن حبان والدارقطني، والنووي في الأذكار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that Friday prayers are witnessed by angels and conveyed to the Prophet until the worshipper finishes; after death, the earth still cannot consume prophets’ bodies, and the Prophet lives sustained.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أكثروا الصلاة علي يوم الجمعة؛ فإنه مشهود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this route strange and interrupted because Ubada ibn Nasi did not meet Abu al-Darda.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r2.anchor: هذا حديث غريب من هذا الوجه، وفيه انقطاع بين عبادة بن نسي وأبي الدرداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة وأبو مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r3.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from Abu Umama and Abu Masud a Prophetic command to increase prayers on the Prophet on Friday night and day; Ibn Kathir says both chains are weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r3.anchor: وقد روى البيهقي من حديث أبي أمامة وأبي مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأمر بالإكثار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r4.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri mursal report says the earth does not consume the body of one addressed by the Holy Spirit; Ibn Kathir grades it mursal hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r4.anchor: سمعت الحسن -هو البصري -يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تأكل الأرض جسد من كلمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r5.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i transmits a mursal Prophetic instruction to increase prayers on him on Friday and its eve.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r5.anchor: وقال الشافعي: أخبرنا إبراهيم بن محمد، أخبرنا صفوان بن سليم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r6.claim: The Friday preacher must bless the Prophet from the pulpit in both sermons, without which the sermons are invalid; Ibn Kathir identifies this as al-Shafi'i and Ahmad's view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r6.anchor: يجب على الخطيب أن يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الجمعة على المنبر في الخطبتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r7.claim: He recommends sending blessings and peace upon the Prophet when visiting his grave.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r7.anchor: يستحب الصلاة والسلام عليه عند زيارة قبره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever greets the Prophet receives his returned greeting after God restores his spirit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p473/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من (9) أحد يسلم علي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's direction not to make homes graves or his grave a festival, but to pray upon him because prayers reach him wherever people are; Abu Dawud alone transmits it and al-Nawawi authenticates it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تجعلوا بيوتكم قبورا، ولا تجعلوا قبري عيدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r2.claim: A man who visited the Prophet's grave each morning explained that he loved to greet him; Ali ibn al-Husayn cited his father and grandfather for the same instruction to pray and greet from anywhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r2.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين بن علي: أن رجلا كان يأتي كل غداة فيزور قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r3.claim: The household report through Ali ibn al-Husayn has an unnamed narrator in its chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r3.anchor: في إسناده رجل مبهم لم يسم (2) وقد روي من وجه آخر مرسلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r4.speaker: الحسن بن الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r4.claim: In a mursal report, al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan sees people at the grave and forbids taking it as a festival, citing that prayers reach the Prophet wherever offered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن الحسن بن علي؛ أنه رأى قوما عند القبر فنهاهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir supposes al-Hasan may have reprimanded the visitors because they were behaving discourteously by raising their voices beyond need.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p474/r5.anchor: فلعله رآهم يسيئون الأدب برفع أصواتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r1.claim: A grave visitor is told that a person in Andalusia is no farther from the Prophet than he is, since the Prophet receives everyone's prayers and blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r1.anchor: يا هذا، ما أنت ورجل بالأندلس منه إلا سواء، أي: الجميع يبلغه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r2.speaker: الحسن بن الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r2.claim: Al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali reports from his father the instruction to pray upon the Prophet wherever one is, since the prayer reaches him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r2.anchor: عن حسن بن حسن بن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنهم، عن أبيه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "صلوا علي حيثما كنتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r3.speaker: أم أنيس بنت الحسن بن علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r3.claim: A report says God appointed two angels who ask forgiveness for anyone who prays upon the Prophet when he is mentioned, and God and His angels answer amen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r3.anchor: عن أم أنيس بنت الحسن بن علي، عن أبيها قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أرأيت قول الله، عز وجل: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the angel report very strange and its chain severely weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r4.anchor: غريب جدا، وإسناده فيه ضعف شديد (8)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God has angels traveling the earth who convey the Muslim community's greetings to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن لله ملائكة سياحين في الأرض، يبلغوني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r6.claim: A report claims that prayers at the Prophet's grave are heard directly and distant prayers are conveyed; Ibn Kathir questions its chain, unique to the abandoned Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi al-Saghir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p475/r6.anchor: تفرد به محمد بن مروان السدي الصغير، وهو متروك، عن الأعمش، عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r1.claim: The authors' school recommends that a pilgrim in ihram pray upon the Prophet after finishing the talbiya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r1.anchor: قال أصحابنا: ويستحب للمحرم إذا لبى وفرغ من تلبيته أن يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r2.speaker: القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r2.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad reports that a man was instructed to pray upon the Prophet whenever he completed his talbiya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r2.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق قال: كان يؤمر الرجل إذا فرغ من تلبيته أن يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على كل حال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r3.claim: Umar instructs pilgrims to perform seven circuits, pray two units at the Station, then make takbirs and supplications at al-Safa and al-Marwa, including praise, blessings on the Prophet, and personal requests; Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and strong.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، عن وهب بن الأجدع قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: إذا قدمتم فطوفوا بالبيت سبعا، وصلوا عند المقام ركعتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r4.claim: Some recommend mentioning blessings on the Prophet alongside God's name at slaughter, taking support from 94:4 and an interpretation that God is never mentioned without the Prophet also being mentioned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r4.anchor: ويستحب الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع ذكر الله عند الذبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r5.claim: The majority rejects that practice, holding that slaughter is a place to mention God alone, like eating, entering, and intercourse, where no Prophetic instruction to bless the Prophet exists.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r5.anchor: وخالفهم في ذلك الجمهور، وقالوا: هذا موطن يفرد فيه ذكر الرب تعالى، كما عند الأكل، والدخول، والوقاع وغير ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r6.claim: A Prophetic report commands prayers upon God's prophets and messengers; Ibn Kathir says its chain contains two weak narrators, Umar ibn Harun and his teacher.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "صلوا على أنبياء الله ورسله؛ فإن الله بعثهم كما بعثني"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r7.claim: He recommends praying upon the Prophet if one's ear rings, provided the report is sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك: أنه يستحب الصلاة عليه عند طنين الأذن، إن صح الخبر في ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r8.speaker: أبو رافع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r8.claim: Abu Rafi reports the instruction to remember and pray upon the Prophet when an ear rings and to say God remembers whoever remembers him well; Ibn Kathir calls the chain strange and questions its authenticity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p476/r8.anchor: عن أبيه أبي رافع (2) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا طنت أذن أحدكم فليذكرني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r1.claim: Writers are said to recommend repeating blessings each time they write the Prophet's name; a report from Ibn Abbas promises continuing reward while the name remains in the book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من صلى علي في كتاب، لم تزل الصلاة جارية له ما دام اسمي في ذلك الكتاب"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r2.speaker: author
