IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Ibn Abbas report is unsound from many routes, as is an Abu Hurayra version; al-Dhahabi suspects fabrication, and versions from Abu Bakr and Ibn Abbas are also invalid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r2.anchor: وليس هذا الحديث بصحيح من وجوه كثيرة، وقد روي من حديث أبي هريرة، ولا يصح أيضا (6)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r3.speaker: الذهبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r3.claim: Al-Dhahabi says he suspects the report about writing blessings is fabricated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r3.anchor: قال الحافظ أبو عبد الله الذهبي شيخنا: أحسبه موضوعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r4.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r4.claim: Al-Khatib reports seeing in Ahmad ibn Hanbal's handwriting that he often wrote the Prophet's name without the blessing in writing, though it reached him that Ahmad said the blessing aloud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477/r4.anchor: قال: رأيت بخط الإمام أحمد بن حنبل، رحمه الله: كثيرا ما يكتب اسم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من غير ذكر الصلاة عليه كتابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r1.claim: Sending blessings as an appendage to blessings on the Prophet's family, wives, or descendants is permissible by consensus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r1.anchor: كما تقدم في الحديث: "اللهم، صل على محمد وآله وأزواجه وذريته"، فهذا جائز بالإجماع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r2.speaker: قائلون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r2.claim: Some allow singling out non-prophets for blessings, citing verses about God's and the angels' blessings, prayers for believers, and Prophetic responses to almsgivers and a woman who requested prayers for herself and her husband.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r2.anchor: فقال قائلون: يجوز ذلك، واحتجوا بقوله: {هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r3.claim: The majority disallows singling out non-prophets because the formula has become a distinctive mark of prophets; they read apparent scriptural examples as supplication, and Ibn Kathir calls this a good approach.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r3.anchor: وقال الجمهور من العلماء: لا يجوز إفراد غير الأنبياء بالصلاة؛ لأن هذا قد صار شعارا للأنبياء إذا ذكروا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r4.claim: Others prohibit it because blessings on non-prophets became a distinctive practice of people of innovation, whose conventions should not be followed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: لا يجوز ذلك؛ لأن الصلاة على غير الأنبياء قد صارت من شعار أهل الأهواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r5.speaker: النووي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r5.claim: The three reported positions are prohibition, mild dislike, or contrary to what is preferable; al-Nawawi says the correct majority position is mild dislike because it is an innovation's emblem.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r5.anchor: حكاه الشيخ أبو زكريا النووي في كتاب الأذكار. ثم قال: والصحيح الذي عليه الأكثرون أنه مكروه كراهة تنزيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r6.speaker: أبو محمد الجويني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r6.claim: Al-Juwayni treats the greeting like blessings: do not use it as an isolated formula for absent non-prophets, while greeting those present is unanimously permitted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p477#2/r6.anchor: وأما السلام فقال الشيخ أبو محمد الجويني من أصحابنا: هو في معنى الصلاة، فلا يستعمل في الغائب، ولا يفرد به غير الأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir notes copyists' tendency to single out Ali with عليه السلام or كرم الله وجهه and says companions should be treated equally in honorifics; the two shaykhs and Uthman deserve them even more.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r1.anchor: أن يفرد علي، رضي الله عنه، بأن يقال: "عليه السلام"، من دون سائر الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says blessings should not be said over anyone but the Prophet; Muslims should instead be prayed for with forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس أنه قال: لا تصح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r3.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r3.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ordered that blessings be reserved for prophets and supplication made generally for Muslims, after storytellers began giving caliphs and rulers formulas like the Prophet's; Ibn Kathir grades the report hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r3.anchor: كتب عمر بن عبد العزيز، رحمه الله: أما بعد، فإن أناسا من الناس قد التمسوا الدنيا بعمل الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r4.speaker: كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r4.claim: Ka'b tells Aisha that seventy thousand angels come by dawn and again by night to surround the Prophet's grave and pray for him, then seventy thousand accompany him at resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p478/r4.anchor: أن كعبا دخل على عائشة، رضي الله عنها، فذكروا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال كعب: ما من فجر يطلع إلا نزل سبعون ألفا من الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p479/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p479/r1.speaker: النووي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p479/r1.claim: Al-Nawawi says one should combine blessings and greeting upon the Prophet rather than say only one, deriving this recommendation from the verse; the fuller formula is to bless him and greet him fully.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p479/r1.anchor: إذا صلى على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فليجمع بين الصلاة والتسليم، فلا يقتصر على أحدهما

JISHUMI:v8p5763/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r1.claim: The common reading has wa-malāʾikatahu in the accusative, coordinated with God’s name as the object of inna.
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: (وملائكته) بالنصب عطفا على اسم الله تعالى

JISHUMI:v8p5763/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the word in the nominative, coordinated with the syntactic position of “God” before inna, as in the variant parsing of al-ṣābiʾūn in 5:69.
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس بالرفع وعطفا على محل قوله: (الله) قبل دخول (إن) عليه

JISHUMI:v8p5763/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r3.claim: Ṣalāh means supplication lexically and a set of acts and remembrances in law; its meaning varies by agent: God’s mercy and praise, angels’ supplication and forgiveness-seeking, the Prophet’s intercession, and the community’s request for instruction by supplication.
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r3.anchor: الصلاة: اسم للدعاء، وفي الشرع: عبارة عن أفعال مخصوصة وأذكار، ثم تختلف فهي من الله الرحمة والثناء

JISHUMI:v8p5763/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r4.claim: Taslim is a supplication for safety.

JISHUMI:v8p5763/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r11.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r11.claim: One parsing supplies an omitted subject for “they send blessings” from God and the angels; Abū ʿAlī says it is omitted only for the angels, since God is mentioned separately out of reverence.
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r11.anchor: قيل: (يصلون) فيه إضمار عن اسم الله وملائكته، وقيل: بل هو إضمار عن الملائكة دون اسم الله

JISHUMI:v8p5763/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r12.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r12.claim: The Prophet corrected a speaker who said “whoever disobeys them both,” instructing him to say “whoever disobeys God and His Messenger,” so they would not be joined under a dual pronoun.
JISHUMI:v8p5763/r12.anchor: من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى، فنهاه رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r1.claim: The nominative reading وَمَلَائِكَتُهُ coordinates with the syntactic position of إن and its subject for the Kufis; Basris explain it by an omitted predicate supplied by يصلون.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r1.anchor: قرىء : ( وملائكته ) بالرفع ، عطفا على محل إن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r2.claim: Believers are to invoke God's blessing and peace upon the Messenger, asking God to show him mercy and grant him peace.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r2.anchor: ومعناه : الدعاء بأن يترحم عليه الله ويسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r3.claim: The author rules that blessing the Prophet is obligatory, then records disagreement over how often the duty applies.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r3.anchor: قلت : بل واجبة ، وقد اختلفوا في حال وجوبها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r4.claim: Some jurists require blessing the Prophet every time he is mentioned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r4.anchor: فمنهم من أوجبها كلما جرى ذكره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r5.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r5.claim: A prophetic report warns that whoever hears the Prophet mentioned without blessing him enters the Fire and is distanced by God; no grading is given.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r5.anchor: من ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي فدخل النار فأبعده الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r6.claim: Some require one blessing per gathering even if the Prophet is mentioned repeatedly, by analogy with prostration at a recitation verse and responding to a sneeze.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r6.anchor: ومنهم من قال : تجب في كل مجلس مرة ، وإن تكرر ذكره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r7.claim: Some require blessing the Prophet at the beginning and end of every supplication.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r7.anchor: وكذلك في كل دعاء في أوله وآخره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r8.claim: Some require blessing the Prophet once in a lifetime, analogously to the obligation to profess the two testimonies.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r8.anchor: ومنهم من أوجبها في العمر مرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r9.claim: The cautious course is to bless the Prophet whenever he is mentioned, in light of the reports.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r9.anchor: والذي يقتضيه الاحتياط . الصلاة عليه عند كل ذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions do not treat blessing the Prophet in ritual prayer as a condition for its validity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r10.anchor: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه لا يرونها شرطا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r11.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r11.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i reports that the Companions considered the tashahhud, including peace upon the Prophet, sufficient.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r11.anchor: وعن إبراهيم النخعي : كانوا يكتفون عن ذلك يعني الصحابة بالتشهد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r12.speaker: الشافعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r12.claim: Al-Shafi'i makes blessing the Prophet in prayer a condition of its validity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r12.anchor: وأما الشافعي رحمه الله فقد جعلها شرطا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r13.claim: By analogy, blessing any believer is permissible, supported by verses saying God blesses believers and directing the Prophet to pray for them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r13.anchor: القياس جواز الصلاة على كل مؤمن ، لقوله تعالى : { هو الذى يصلى عليكم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r14.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r14.claim: The passage begins introducing a further prophetic saying as evidence for blessing believers, but its wording falls beyond this segment.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r15.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r15.claim: A prophetic report says God appointed two angels: when a Muslim blesses the Prophet they ask forgiveness and God and His angels say amen; if the Muslim omits it, they curse him and God and His angels say amen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p566#3/r15.anchor: إن الله وكل بي ملكين فلا أذكر عند مسلم فيصلي علي إلا قال ذانك الملكان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r1.claim: God's prayer is His praise of the Prophet before the angels; the angels' prayer is supplication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن صلاة الله تعالى عليه ثناؤه عليه عند الملائكة , وصلاة الملائكة الدعاء , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r2.claim: God's prayer means forgiveness for the Prophet; the angels seek forgiveness for him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن صلاة الله تعالى عليه المغفرة له , وصلاة الملائكة الاستغفار له , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r3.claim: God's prayer means mercy, and angels pray for him; this is also Ata ibn Abi Rabah's view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r3.anchor: قاله الحسن , وهو معنى قول عطاء بن أبي رباح

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says their prayer means blessing the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r4.anchor: الرابع : أن صلاتهم عليه أن يباركوا عليه ؟ قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r5.claim: Ka'b ibn Ujra asked the Prophet how to pray for him; the Prophet taught a formula blessing Muhammad and his family as Abraham and his family were blessed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r5.anchor: روى عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى قال : لقيني كعب بن عجرة فقال : ألا أهدي لك هدية سمعتها من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r6.speaker: أبو العباس ثعلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r6.claim: Thalab explains “God bless Muhammad” as asking increased blessing and mercy; other interpretations also apply.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r6.anchor: قال أبو العباس ثعلب : معنى قولنا اللهم صل على محمد أي زد محمدا بركة ورحمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r7.claim: One sense of submitting to the Prophet is obeying his command.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r7.anchor: أحدهما : سلموا لأمره بالطاعة له تسليما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r8.claim: A second sense is invoking peace upon him by greeting him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r8.anchor: وسلموا عليه بالدعاء له تسليما أي سلاما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r9.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r9.claim: After this verse Muslims asked what they would receive; then 33:43 was revealed saying God and His angels bless them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p421/r9.anchor: حكى مقاتل قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية قال المسلمون

MUJAHID:v2p520#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p520#2/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MUJAHID:v2p520#2/r1.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says God's prayer is His praise of the Prophet before the angels, while the angels' prayer is their supplication for him.
MUJAHID:v2p520#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية ﴿ إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي ﴾ قال صلاة الله عليه ثناؤه عليه عند الملائكة

MUQATIL:33:55-56/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r3.claim: God's ṣalāt on the Prophet means forgiveness, while the angels' ṣalāt means asking forgiveness for him.
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r3.anchor: أما صلاة الرب عز وجل فالمغفرة للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:33:55-56/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r4.claim: The command for believers to pray for the Prophet means asking God to forgive him.
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r4.anchor: { يأيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه } يعنى استغفروا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:33:55-56/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r5.speaker: المسلمون
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r5.claim: When the verse was revealed, Muslims told the Messenger that it was for him and asked what was for them.
MUQATIL:33:55-56/r5.anchor: قال المسلمون: هذه لك، يا رسول الله، فما لنا؟

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r1.claim: The command can be fulfilled by saying, O God, bless Muhammad, or May God bless Muhammad.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r1.anchor: أى قولوا اللهم صل على محمد أو صلى الله على محمد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r2.claim: Salutation means asking God to grant Muhammad peace, or submitting fully to his command and judgment.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r2.anchor: أى قولوا اللهم سلم على محمد أو انقادوا لامره وحكمه انقيادا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r3.speaker: محمد ﷺ
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r3.claim: The Prophet said two angels are assigned to him: when a Muslim blesses him they ask God to forgive that person and God says amen; if not, they pray against the person and God again says amen.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r3.anchor: وسئل عليه السلام عن هذه الآية فقال إن الله وكل بى ملكين فلا أذكر عند عبد مسلم فيصلى على إلا قال ذانك الملكان غفر الله لك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r4.speaker: الطحاوي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r4.claim: Al-Ṭaḥāwī holds that invoking blessings on the Prophet is obligatory once.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r4.anchor: ثم هى واجبة مرة عند الطحاوى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r5.speaker: الكرخي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r5.claim: Al-Karkhī holds that the blessing is obligatory whenever the Prophet's name is mentioned.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r5.anchor: وكلما ذكر اسمه عند الكرخى وهو الاحتياط

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r6.claim: Invoking blessings whenever the Prophet is mentioned is precautionary and the view of the majority.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r6.anchor: كلما ذكر اسمه عند الكرخى وهو الاحتياط وعليه الجمهور

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r7.claim: There is no objection to including the Prophet's family when blessings are sent upon him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r7.anchor: وان صلى على غيره على سبيل التبع كقوله صلى الله على النبى وآله فلا كلام فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r8.claim: Separately invoking blessings on another member of the Prophet's household is disliked and, in Nasafi's polemic, a distinctive practice of the Rāfiḍīs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p314/r8.anchor: وأما اذا أفرد غيره من أهل البيت بالصلاة فمكروه وهو من شعائر الروافض
